comment: Trail was pretty easy and flat for the first 3KM and then the last 1.5KM it was all rock climbing 🥲 Beautiful views though, I would do those hike again. Bring bug spray, hiking poles and lots of water!
Dog friendly right up to the rock scramble to get to the crack viewpoint. Very difficult to get a dog up there unless you carry them.
Stunning ! This hike is quite easy until about 1.5 before the view point then it gets pretty rough
Last half kilometer was very tricky but overall, amazing pay off!
Great trail!! Started to incline around the 2.6km mark. The scrambling started around the 3.5km mark but was doable even after it had rained in the morning. Well worth the trek!

Such a great trail! First ~2.5km is pretty flat then the remainder (around 1.5km) has some elevation! You only really have to scramble for the last bit of the hike (only around ~300m) It’s moderately difficult but nothing crazy! The view at the end is so worth it!
Great hike! Beautiful view at the top! The rocky part is hard for dogs, ours needed some help
Very rough rocky terrain near top

Short and steep hike. Beautiful views. I went on a Wednesday at 8am and it there was tons of people. Everyone was super friendly though. Bugs were too bad past the first part of the trail. No bathrooms. There is a spot in the beginning of the hike, past the bridge where you can swim in the lake. I did it on my way back, it was very refreshing. There is massive boulder field so make sure you are comfortable navigating that. If it’s too short of a hike you can go past the crack to one of the lakes, that’s what I originally planned but was feeling well so turned back after reaching a second view point. Cell service is spotty so don’t rely on my stats.

Beautiful trail - as you get closer to the top, it can be harder to spot the trail markers so All Trails GPS was invaluable.

Saw a very unbothered black bear and also some raptors/corvids at the top, soaring over the lakes - gorgeous.

Stop littering! 
Trail is great has beautiful views 
Bring bug spray and water

This was a beautiful hike. We thoroughly enjoyed it. We brought our medium sized dog with us on the hike. There was only a few spots it was tough for him , which he needed lifting for. It is a great hike with a lot of rewarding views , definitely worth the effort it demands.
Very hard summit awesome views and trail
Pretty flat and forested for the first 2.5km! Straight up towards last 1.5km to the top. 10/10 hike! 100% worth it!!
Most satisfying trail in Ontario!
SO FUN!!! 8.6km round trip

Easy for 3km then elevation picked up in the last 1km to the top - be prepared to scramble up some rocks but fairly easy if you call yourself agile or athletic. 
otherwise still don’t be discouraged there’s plenty of other ways to get up the steeper parts it’s just I love to climb and challenge myself lol

Download an offline trail map on your phone before starting the hike

Have plenty of water

Pack some snacks
Great hike! With good spots to swim at!
Easy hike on 3/4 part of it but the rocky parts,1/4, were hard. It was a fun hike! Love it!
Great Ontario trail!
Nice views at the top but very steep, be careful with climb!!

The first 3/4 is covered bush trail. The last quarter is where it gets rocky and difficult. But the view is worth it! There is a bridge you have to cross in the first hour that is submerged in the water, so be prepared your feet may get wet. Took us almost 4 hours. No bathrooms though and zero cell service once you get into Killarney.

Most of the trail is quite easy, there is some elevation but nothing crazy. The crack is climbing up some rocks (which also means climbing back down!) 
Often a wet trail until you start the incline so wear appropriate footwear! Went June 30 this year and bugs were still quite bad, bug suit/shirt and spray highly recommended because you will get eaten alive! As well bring lots of water this time of year. Have gone in late September and the bugs were obviously significantly less.
Super fun and easy hike, I have no idea why people are saying it’s hard because it’s very easy.
Muddy and bugs
Incredible view from the top.  Went In June while thunder-storming and it was a crazy amount of mosquitoes. You need to be fully covered, wear a BUG NET!
Great trail and great view at the top. It is possible with children under 7 but have to be prepared and know your child capabilities.
Bring some stretchy pants
View is good. Don’t come in June, mosquitoes are crazy
Beautiful views at the top. Wore a bug net and bug spray and there wasn’t a problem.
A lot of mosquitos during this tome so bring a net for the woods area, but once u make it out of the woods they arent a problem anymore

there is a designated parking area for this trail. You have to book ahead of time on line. 
The hike is not difficult. The climb up the  crack is  technicaly harder due to the larger jumble boulders that have collapsed into the crack. 
You definitely need bug spray.
Amazing trail! Challenging but rewarding. If it’s bug season, a bug net is essential. Mosquitoes are bad in the early sections.
Lots of bugs!

Beautiful hike up this little but a tough one! Never attempt in June without proper misquote/fly gear. Else life will be miserable. Apart from that, totally worth the view and the fresh strong breeze of air up in the mountains! Unmatched and amazing! And ofcourse, carry your bear spray cuz it definitely is a proper backcountry!

I started the hike at 3am to catch the sunrise from the summit. Hiked to the summit fully in the dark. Had a couple small turnarounds, but the trail was marked well enough that I was fine even at night. And the view is incredible!

Had to wait a few hours to see if a spot would open up for me to park. This trail is marked as hard but I would say it’s more of a moderate trail. Other than that it was a great trail, with great conditions and amazing views.
The bugs here were absolutely outrageous bring your bug net or don’t bother
Definitely a quick easy trail, saw two groups carrying babies
Take your water bottle with you
Bring snacks and water! Wear good shoes, some bouldering involved and can be slippery. 8km not 99km
Easy hike with a gentle elevation and some light scrambling near the top at the crack. Beautiful views and absolutely worth it.
some scrambling but overall fun!

Amazing trail with great views at the top. I did this trail with an amazing local guide from Toronto, Javier (Toronto Eco Adventures). The beginning section of the trail is mostly flat with gradual inclines. After that it starts gaining elevation fast. The last section, which is mostly rock has several sections with steep inclines. Must wear proper hiking shoes else you will risk an injury to your feet/ankle due to the uneven terrain. The hike is totally worth it for the amazing panoramic views at the top.
We did the hike during a short break in a 2 day rainstorm; enjoyed amazing views of valley fog amongst the fall foliage!  Beautiful terrain!
Such a great hike! Trail was great, easy to walk. If doing it in the winter Will need crampons (ice cleats) as some parts of the trail going up near the mountain top. 10/10 recommend.

I have done this hike numerous times in the summer and fall, but never in the winter! The snow was deep, but packed to nicely with a very obvious trail to follow.  Definitely need spikes to scramble to the top! Difficult, and slippery, but well worth the view as always. If you are going with dogs, as I did, bring a longer leash with you, so they can find their footing while you find yours! Great hike, and will be back again this winter at least once more.

if anyone finds a tan beanie on the 3-4th segments please let me know lol

apart from that, amazing hike, no complaints
Amazing winter conditions. Snow blanket over the entire trail, roughly ~30 cm of snow. Cleats would be good to have for the final summit, but overall there’s fresh snow fall.

This was a cool hike! Climbing up through the boulders made me feel like a kid again. The view at the top was absolutely stunning! I can only imagine what it would be like with the fall colors! The trail in places was a bit muddy, but that's expected this time of season. Really enjoyed! Awesome experience!

Beautiful hike, definitely challenging if you’re not a regular hiker. We got to the end, looked at the rocks, and said “Is that the trail?”, (It was indeed the trail). Worth the hike up for the views!
This hike was hard. I didn’t even make it to the top.

Although this trail is rated as moderate by All Trails and difficult by the park, you can actually walk at least 2-3 km in while the trail is easy. Sometime after that it becomes moderate to slightly difficult. No matter how far you go, it’s beautiful. 
In late October it had been raining quite a bit so many wet areas. None that were impassable.
Went on a rainy day definitely slippery and windy. But still doable
Amazing trail and views.worth it trying.
We did the trail on a rainy day and be careful of the very slippery conditions and be sure to dress appropriately and wear proper foot wear

Amazing trail with amazing views! The perfect amount of challenging and fun. Well marked and easy to navigate. Took us about an hour up and an hour down. Proper footwear is a must! Be prepared to climb up and over large rocks. The trail was quite busy still so ensure you book in advance. Overall, an absolute must do!!

(note that we hiked this trail in mid-October, in dry and mild weather).  The Ontario Parks website states that this trail is one of, if not the, most difficult trails in the province.  It isn't very difficult.  I'd say a 3/5 in difficulty.  The only difficult part is near the end, right at the crack itself, where you need to scramble up over ancient rock falls (you can wear garden gloves to help).  Most of the rest of the trail is over well travelled and sturdy paths without much loose stones.  All the loose, ankle rolling stones had been removed from the main paths.  We saw many older hikers having a wonderful time returning from the top.
Gorgeous fall colors

Left around 11am after a rainy night, we were warned that the rocks are going to be slippery. Parking lot was not too crowded when we left, and only moderate crowd on the trail for a Saturday on long weekend. I would say the hike is easy to moderate, only the last 150m were strenuous everything else being a flat forested walk. Views up at the summit are gorgeous, fall colors were spectacular

This was ana amazing trail with Beautiful fall views. The first half is a straightforward walk which wasn't that much fun. However the second portion of the trail was where I rated this 5 stars. Elevation gain, scrambling through large rocks boulders and eventually through the crack. It was an adrenaline rush at times. The last part just before going through the crack was where people were making their own route to the top. Need to be very careful with sturdy shoes that have good grip. 

Once you are at the top, you get stunning views of Killarney and the La Cloche Mountain range. We took almost 30-45 min break at the top before making our way back down. 10/10 experience.
Try it, you will see it with your own eyes.

Challenging as the elevation rose and the scramble looked intimidating but slow and steady got me up and through. The views were worth it though and I was thrilled to complete for the first time at the age of 56. Would highly recommend going in the Fall for the absolutely beautiful colours.
So beautiful! Challenging climb over boulders but worth it

Holy views, a very powerful experience! So far, my favourite hike in Ontario. The trail up offers a variety of terrains to experience. Every change in elevation writes a different story for your eyes, knees, hands and legs. As you begin,  enjoy a long leisurely stroll through a beautiful forest peppered with stunning birch and hemlock stands. Stroll over a bridge that the beavers have claimed as their own, take a quick dip in the Kakakise lake with a water snake(or not), continue up the mountainside using roots as your foothold to suddenly come upon the beautiful white quartzite. But wait, why is it called ‘the crack’, well , you’ll know when you see it! Easier to navigate than you might think, but then again, the mind is a powerful controller! Steady, one foot, hand, or all fours if needed. You will ascend to the top elated and energized by the reward of a view which is beyond the capturing capacity of any camera. Sit, snack and let it all sink it. After a while, think about the decent, then linger a while more, it’s ok to be at peace, to feel calm, to know serenity. Take in the views of the lakes, Georgian Bay, Manitoulin, the deciduous and evergreen trees, the sky, the rock, it’s stunning! Crab on down and reflect on how fortunate you are to be able to have this experience! Hike on!
I GOT ENGAGED

Beautiful and fun trail, but gets very busy - both parking lot and trail included. For a better experience, try getting started with the hike in the morning and aim to be finished the 3.5-4hr trip (depending on skill, rest periods, etc.) by early afternoon. 
Regardless, one of Ontarios best day hikes, in my opinion!! Very unique.
Beautiful, fun and at times challenging trail when climbing the rocks to the crack. Incredible views.
Don’t listen to the parks staff, park on the road instead of walking 3k from the other parking lot
Relatively difficult but kids dogs and all sorts on the trail, so it's doable for all.
As always such a beautiful trail with great vistas to look at!  Well marked and taken care of.
Worth the hike
Be prepared. Difficult scrambling at the end!! Bring enough water, a hat, snacks, and ideally hiking boots with some ankle support.

Beautiful view worth the effort - small parking lot.  About 2km of easy- moderate then gets quite difficult.  Wouldn’t want to do it in wet conditions.  We were here beginning of October, sunny day and it was perfect.  Glad we did it.  Saw many dogs, going up probably easier for them than going down

Probably one of the most fun hikes I've ever been on. The changing terrain keeps this interesting and the final scramble takes 5-7 mins at most. And the view! Truly a stunning hike. The fall colours are starting to peak through.
Amazing fall hike!
Difficult trail, nicely marked and fantastic views! Rocky climbs - loved it
Most of the trail was easy to moderate. The final portion up thThe Crack was hard.
Trying to beat my summit times with a full pack

An accomplishment for sure to be with a group of mature hiking women and we all made it!! 
As seasoned hikers we were prepared for the roots and rocks. The last climbing part was challenging but doable. It was worth the effort.

Oof - do NOT over estimate your hiking ability. Pretty easy hike up until “the crack”. It looks pretty intimidating but with time and proper footing it is manageable and worth the multiple lookout points at the top. Descending the crack felt easier but was a little spooky. Overall, happy to have done this hike. Our 10 year old son managed the hike better than us ! Haha
The Crack part of the Trail is very challenging,  wear proper hiking boots or shoes
Novice hiker. Perfect trail. Well maintained. Rock scramble a little challenging but overall a great hike! Worth the views at the top
Definitely recommend coming earlier in the morning. By noon it is very busy and parking is hard to find
Great trail, quick easy hike. You can trail run this easily. Lots of people later in day, you should come early in morning (6-7am).
Great views
First 3 km are easy flat hike, further in the difficulty increases. There’s a bit of scrambling but our dog was able to manage. Beautiful 360 view at the top.
First third of trail easy walking, second third narrow trail but in good shape, last third hill climb over rock and talus slope ( difficult section particularly on the way down).

This was a beautiful hike, but wouldn’t consider it hard. The last km or so is walking and climbing up rocks, with the last couple hundred meters doing a bit of scrambling, but even as we hiked through the rain on the rock, we would considerate intermediate, many dogs were able to make it up the crack to the top of the trail.
Slippery when wet, lots of rock scramble
Fun hike, the scramble up and down the rocks is a highlight.  The view is amazing.  Rained a bit on the way up, rocks can get slippery.

The first two thirds of the trail is pretty straight forward (two track and rolling).  The climb up that last km is very much a rock scramble at the end, but very doable.  Far less intimidating than expected.  Dog-friendly enough - we took a 9lb chihuahua and a 16 lb terrier up and they did fine with a few lifts (getting down was a bit more challenging for them).  A harness with a handle would be helpful for larger dogs.  Incredible views at the top - well worth the effort.  Took us just over 3 hrs total with about a 30 min break at the top (late 40s, experienced hikers).  Definitely recommend good shoes and at least one trekking pole really helped on the way down.
Great conditions, no bugs

This one took 2 hours to complete and that’s with taking photos at the peak and chatting with people. I’d definitely list this one as moderate rather than hard. Beautiful views and some basic rock scrambling towards the top. Worth checking out.

Top notch trail, harder/longer than listed but 100% worth the views. Climbing required, wear proper shoes. Children and seniors were doing this trail as well so don’t be intimidated. Takes about 3 hours with breaks, pictures, snacks etc.
Permits need to be purchased a few days in advance on busy weekends
Great view at the top. Took about 4 hours with a lunch break at the peak. Scramble for the last 1
Great hike, amazing views at the top. Scramble was fun.
Fantastic hike. It was about sunny with a nice breeze and  20°C for the entire hike. Started about 9:30 and we were back at our campsite just after 1pm.

This was a challenging but amazing hike. 2/3 is a path through the woods. It’s the last 1/3 that is very challenging - scrabbling up rocks and increase in elevation. Absolutely worth it but be prepared with proper footwear and climb safely.

“The Crack” was a very eventful hike! Starts off easy and gradually gets more difficult. Lots of cool scenery’s and fun rock scaling throughout the hike. I personally would have said it is a more advanced hike but I saw tones of families doing this hike with their young kids.
Excellent hike ..
Trail was a little wet today, but the view at the top was amazing.
Great views at Crack, not much after that.

Trail conditions were good today! Only 3 cars in the parking lot when I showed up at 8:15am but when leaving at 11am, it was packed so ideally come early. 

The hike is just under 8km and I’d rate it as moderate. The first 2.5km is relatively flat and then it goes pretty much uphill from there until you’re at the top at 4km!
I loved hiking this. The trail is well maintained and climbing up the rocky areas was a lot of fun. It is definitely a workout, but so fulfilling when you get to the top!

The trail is in good shape (and is actually less muddy than usual thanks to the drought conditions). But on the other side of that, the lakes are pretty dry and less pretty and the humidity makes this normally fun climb almost unbearable. Bring a hat and a ton of water this summer.

I concur with others that proper hiking footwear is a must, and a decent fitness level for climbing up and then back down the very challenging/technical section. Ditto on bringing water, a snack, and bug spray. Took me 4 hours total, spending time up top for gorgeous views, pics, and conversing with other hikers. I'm in my 60s, fairly fit, and managed, but really took my time. On the trail, I saw people with sandals or other bad footwear, families with toddlers carrying their blankies or stuffies, and even a little kid in pajamas! I'm guessing they likely turned back as the trail got increasingly difficult...at least I hope so. I personally had a blast!
Challenging yet not that difficult

Thoroughly enjoyable clambering up to and through the crack with a beautiful view as the reward!

With breaks, view pics, snacks and such it took us 3.5 hours.
Be aware, this trail is longer than the posted length at the trailhead parking lot!
The wide trail at the beginning and end is easy to navigate. The climb is very steep and technical. A difficult trail so you need to be prepared for that climb.
This is a difficult hike. You have to climb large rocks. Please wear good footwear. It's exhausting and strenuous.

We went a bit later in the day, not crowded at all! It was a bit buggy so definitely bring bug spray. Not suitable for kids or people with mobility difficulties that impact climbing/balance. Absolutely beautiful, challenging hike
Amazing views! Buggy (July)!

amazing trail with amazing views! Definitely go early to enjoy the quiet, because it gets crowded later in the day. absolutely awesome and super fun to scale the rocky terrain, too. bring at least 2L of water as well, an absolute need!
The view was great
The way back was really hard, but the view was perfect and I would go again. Also worth mentioning is that this was the crack trail.
Amazing trail!!! The views are amazing! The trek up was so fun and not too tricky!

Good level of challenge for families. Definitely provided some challenge. Not easy for sure. But if you are in reasonable shape it is fun and reasonably demanding. Cool rock formations along the way and a great view at the top
really great trail, very frequented by me

Not scary or what I’d consider hard vs a lot of other trails on this app. Minimal elevation gain, no scary cliffs. There were more kids than adults on this trail. Fun scramble and nice views for Ontario.
Very rock and steep the last part.
Gotta pay attention follow the markings. Sometimes they hide otherwise incredible hike.

We hiked it in probably under two hours (to the top) with our very able-bodied border-collie-heeler cross. I loved every part of this trail and we didn't find it too diffilicult. The first part is beautiful forest and lake views, where our dog stopped to play in the cool mountain water. We then continued hiking and it truly gets progressively steeper as you go the back half of the trail, until you are climbing about 60-70 degree angle over pretty big boulders. But then you get to the top and it's the most beautiful view I've seen east of the Rockies and north of Old Rag. (Haven't been to the Adirondacks, though. Still...) It was really beautiful and so well worth the climb, which was a good workout for sure but not impossible. Just keep going and don't give up!
It northern Ontario in July. Bugs were awful, trial was muddy but the views were all worth it.

Rigorous hike with a fair bit of vertical, particularly at the final approach to the peak of “the Crack,” where you are essentially all-fours scrambling - carefully! The trail has beautiful scenery after the first 20 minutes or so. The distance given on the Ontario Parks site is 6km…not accurate! The time was about right; we did it in about 3 hours and 45 minutes with water and photo stops and a lunch break at the top (many pretty spots for a picnic) as 3 moderately fit adults close to 50, and one almost 13-year old.

The white La Cloche highlands are unique, like nothing else I’ve seen in Ontario. 

Killarney is a stunner…but in mid-July, woof! The bugs! Would love to do this in the Fall.

Hiked this one on an unfortunately foggy day but by far the longest hike I’ve been on. With stops, pics, eating and water breaks it was around 3.5-4 hours of hiking. Some say it’s dog friendly but I would not agree at all. I saw multiple people bringing their dogs large and small dogs up and trying to forced their large dog up the bouldering section towards the peak. Good luck getting your dog down after that

Easy to walk paths and nice lookouts first 75% of the forest trail and just a bit moderate last 25% of boulders and sharpen stones before you appear at the highest point of the trail, in the middle of it. Good place to have a rest, snack, and understand how big and beautiful the World around you :) Don't sleep to much! Start as early as you can if you don't want to see a lot of people on the trail and on the top of the Crack!!! Sunday 8:40 am was too late to start. Estimated time was 4 hours for both sides, but I did my way back in 50 minutes just walking pretty fast, but not running.
It was great hike

Steep rock climbing for a long time.
Flies, mosquitoes, bees and other bugs

First 3 km’s are easy. After that it’s all uphill. Keep going until it tells you to turn back. Amazing views, well worth the push. Solo hiked it fine with about 3 hours and 15 minutes of walking (there and back) plus spent an hour or so at the top
Total distance is 10 kms due to detour
Fun hike and climbing, awesome views, morning is worse for mosquitoes after 11am is much better.

This is a fun hike that I definitely wouldn't categorize as hard. Most of it is flat until you get to the rocks and even then it's easily navigated if you've done any sort of hiking before. My 7 year and 4 year old chihuahua mixes crushed it no problem. Also not sure why people are complaining so much about the bugs, I'd say it was an average amount. Advise doing this one early morning before the crowds so you don't get stuck behind a bunch of people on the ascent/descent.

Trail reads more true moderate for those that hike regularly. The first 2 km is essentially a flat path (but beautiful). The next 1.5 km is moderate to high moderate. The scramble is why the trail is rated hard, and it is a challenging bit of the trail. My 7 year old dog and I were able to do it fine; make sure to wear the proper footwear! The rating is likely hard because the trail is more popular, I went kitted out expecting a BC hard/hard-moderate - no need! Overall absolutely gorgeous and fun trail! Lots of little side paths/off chutes on the rock to explore.

Trail was a bit confusing once you got to the rocks, definitely had to check our map to get back on track. We got hit with heavy rain on the way down, the trail does get super muddy and flooded quickly. The view was super nice, but like others say, bug spray or netting is 100% needed as we got bit all over even with reapplying. Rock scramble is doable but experience is needed, or super careful footing as rocks are sharp and slippery at times for beginners
This is a beautiful trail, but definitely hard on the knees. Hiking boots is a must. Lots of bugs and mosquitoes on the trail today.
The beginning of the trail is easy and could be done by bike. It’s not hard. Just take your time on the big rocks leading to the crack. Amazing views at the top.

Great trail and worth the view! 
Make sure to follow the live view of the trail so you make it to the very top! 
Full of mosquitos & black flies and pretty muddy (rained the day before)! Bring your bug nets/spray and hiking shoes or boats! 
Would recommend children 12+ as there is some climbing and step rocks. 
Definitely will be back!

The trail is good. 
Better to have mosquitoes or bug repellent. 
And bring your food have a good lunch at the top with an epic view.
Beautiful day at the crack. Hikes in from Killarney lake portage. Not a difficult trip from George lake campground with a canoe.
Second time doing this trail, love it as always, and very gorgeous once again:)
Must have hiking shoes or boots
Went on Saturday, too many mosquitoes, need the nets and being doused in spray. Forest is pretty and then a little scrambled at the end. Nice trail for Ontario standards
Great well maintained trail. Sat and had lunch at the lookout point. Beautiful view. There were a lot of mosquitoes and some muddy parts (had rained for a few days before we went)

Mosquitos were bad but the trail is great, easy parking and gorgeous views at the peak. The rock scramble is a little tough but doable, wear good shoes that grow on slippery rocks and protect your ankles.
Climb is worth the view.
The last section to the top is rocky and challenging, wear good hiking shoes, be prepared to climb.

Very enjoyable trail with an amazing view at the end! The "hard" rating given to this trail is very accurate. If you have poor endurance or things like bad knees I'd suggest avoiding this trail or planning to take a lot longer than average in order to pace yourself. It has many very challenging features. You have to climb steep rocky cliff faces both going up them and then later back down them. 
The trail is marked by arrows, but referencing the map on All trails can be helpful to make sure you stay on course. We had a couple times where we missed an arrow and got a minute or two off track and followed the GPS to get back on route.

Great views, but too many mosquitoes!

The trail has beautiful scenery, but the mosquitoes were terrible. I used a lot of bug spray, but it didn’t help much. I really wish I had brought a mosquito net. I got so many bites on my face and arms. Be prepared if you go!
Bugs were pretty bad at the start and a bug net was necessary.  Great hike overall and a great view at the end!
Don't even consider it without a bug net

Nice. If you are at killarney definitely go.    Nice views from the lookout,  the scramble to the top is fun. Trail well marked, starts out with 1.5km rather mundane stroll along an old road, then follows a nice little lake for a while. By far the best part is the rocky outcrop and bit of a scramble.  Could be a little slippery when wet.  View from top lookout is very nice, not jaw droppingly spectacular though. I think the crack is a mite overrated as a hike. So 4 stars

Parking is just 7km from killarney privincial park. You need a reservation so make sure yoy grt your ticket first from the park. - not to busy I did it at 7am and only saw one other person on the trail. The average time is 4 hours but if you're not stopping until the top you can complete it in 2 1/2 without breaks. The mosquitoes are pretty brutal ( june ) so wear bugspray.  The trail is pretty easy going until you ascend to the top cliff. Some pretty steep rock climbing near the summit. Amazing view from the top and a few great stops along the way.
We saw a bear. Tonnes of black flies at summit.

More of a moderate hike as long as you’re comfortable with a bit of scrambling up some rocks towards the end. Not super strenuous but definitely fun. Spectacular view at the top. Absolutely swarmed with mosquitoes which can be distracting to the point of missing a step. Bug spray was essential and a mosquito net would have been very helpful. No bathrooms. Couldn’t figure out where to find the nearest ones.
The bugs were horrible

May 31, trail was a little muddy, but only in a couple spots, overall was no problem to walk on. The black flies were out of control, if I were to come back I’d for sure bring a bug net. My face, hands, neck were all bit and if it was warmer and I was wearing shorts I bet my legs would’ve been bad too. 

It definitely is a moderate to difficult hike. The most difficult part is the end incline towards the view and you’re going up a pretty steep and jagged section. Would highly recommend wearing hiking footwear or something with lots of grip. The view is incredible, a must do.
Great hike on a great day! Still muddy in parts but drying up. Great time of year to hike it because there are so few people.
Very fun day hike. More challenging rock climbing to get to the peak. great views from high up!

Absolutely stunning hike, amazing views of all kinds. Be prepared for bugs and a bit of scrambling. Parking permits must be reserved 5 days in advance. Active trail, you’ll likely see lots of people but not all in once spot, interactions are quite spread out. It’s busier in the morning and early afternoons.
Lots of bugs, but otherwise a great and beautiful trail.
Nice and cool. Perfect day for a hike. Bugs not an issue due to wind, also they are just swarming not biting yet. Clear skies made for great views.
Great conditions, a little buggy

Different trail conditions and views, wooded, rocky,  ups  and downs etc. Don’t forget to bring refreshing snacks to eat while relaxing in the summit. Hard for dogs on the last climb towards the summit.
The views are amazing from the top. Enjoy but take care. Recommended a very good kind of hiling shoes.

Absolutely fantastic trail. It was definitely very challenging navigating the rocky sections as you had to give your full attention to where you place your feet and hands so you maintain your balance. We were very fortunate that the rocks were mostly dry. I wouldn’t attempt this if the rocks are completely wet. I went with a tour guide (Javier) from EcoAdventures in Toronto who made this whole experience possible as a day trip since they looked after the driving and gave very helpful guidance in navigating the trail. If I wasn’t using them you definitely want to have your AllTrails app on with the downloaded map. It is well marked but it can be difficult to see the markers during the rocky section. There were muddy sections in the beginning part but there were ways to navigate them. It was buggy especially during the rocky sections. They didn’t seem to be biters but I certainly ate quite a few. I loved eating my lunch at the top and the views were absolutely breathtaking even on a cloudy day. The rock, lakes, trees were amazing. There wasn’t any washrooms. You definitely need to make sure you had your parking pass( arrange online prior to going since cell reception is not available until you are on top of the mountain). Park staff were checking vehicles. I would also try to avoid peak times because you don’t want to feel rushed when you are going up or down the rocky sections. Though we saw dogs on the trail I would be hesitant to bring a dog because there are so many areas where they could get hurt. I wouldn’t want to be carrying them since you need your hands. I am 61 with knee sensitivity and bunions which can hurt. I was so happy that I did this when I did. I was happy to have my backpack with water easily accessible. The bridge and boardwalks are all available. Lots of roots but also soft ground cover felt good on the feet. It took us about 3 hours to complete.
Great hike, not too muddy and minimal bugs before noon
Beauty trail. A little bouldering towards the top. Lots of fun

Definitely bring plenty of water. There were two of us, and we used up all 2 liters, even in mid-May. We were blessed with beautiful weather, not too much sun, and no rain or wind. The hike itself was really easy for the first 2 km; then you will start seeing rocky inclines. Near the top, you will need to be on all fours and climb slowly. The view was absolutely rewarding—a breathtaking view of the granite stones and mountains. If you have time, I recommend doing the other trails in the area as well. We did the Chikanishing Trail and Granite Ridge Trail; both were great, with nice views, and much easier than the Crack.
Bridge was washed out. Turned away by park staff at River crossing. They were working to get it cleared and back up.

The hike is definitely worth doing, you need to buy tickets for the park in advance (we did not have reception at the parking). The hike was a bit muddy and the bridge is partially washed away. You can walk around the mud in most places and get over the water without getting wet feet using some logs. As soon as you go uphill the mud disappears and it is a bit of climbing the rocks to get up. Beautiful views at the top
Difficult hike , lot of climbing on lose rocks .  Beautiful view though
Trails very muddy in some spots and bridge was under water . Definitely worth it foe the view

Great hike! No mosquitos. Very wet winter though so parts of the bridge(s) are submerged in water. Very doable hike if you wear waterproof shoes. Some snow present but walkable in normal hiking shoes since it's already melting

Beautiful day at Killarney.  Trail is very muddy intermittently during the first 2km, I recommend bringing some good waterproof hiking shoes.  The water is currently very high and half of the bridge is underwater.  There is logs and branched placed over top of the bridge to keep you from getting a soaker, this part is a bit tricky.  Other than that trail is beautiful!
Views were perfect for an Easter Sunday hike. Low ground was very snowy/icy/slippery, but no ice up high! Viewpoint got busy.

beautiful trail! as of April 19th, most of it is still snowy/icy, so prepare accordingly. you will likely also need changes of socks, as many parts currently require crossing water. the views are 100% worth it
Bridge was flooded but logs were helpful to cross! still slightly icy and snowy but otherwise beautiful. The weather was perfecttttttttt, ended the hike with a woodpecker making its home, so lovely
plan ahead to make sure you’ll get sunshine and not fog lol

Great trail! Bring sturdy shoes, lots of water, snacks and trekking poles! The climb to the top was not too bad, just gotta be careful when going over rocks. Feel free to use your hands while climbing! The payoff at the top is worth the climb!
Trail was well packed, a little water at the bridge, recommend cleats as there is some ice in the very last section of the trail on the rocks

Did this hike this past summer in July. It was one of my favourite hikes I have ever done. Be sure to bring enough water, especially if it is a warm day. Once you reach the first set of rocks to walk and climb on the trail markers can be a bit difficult to find sometimes. Also you need good shoes for this as you end up climbing very large rocks at the end. It took us about 4 hours with a 30-40 lunch break at the top.
The trails real nice right now! Hard packed
The trail was snow covered knee deep near the top. Great work out!

October 17th, 2024.                                                                      Five years since my first hike of The Crack and it still reigns as one of the best day hikes in Ontario. The stark white of the quartz hillsides, are stunning when set in the autumnal scenery. And the main views at the top are almost unparalleled in the province.
Watch out for water holes…. One bridge partially under water…
Great trail, well marked. Not as difficult as we had anticipated.
Unbelievable day!  Gorgeous sunshine. Crisp clear air. Fantastic experience. 10/10

Stunning views and great trail. Many twists and turns on various terrain. Was a bit intimidating going up the last stretch of the trail with my dog but she did great. If Marv (dog) wasn’t as agile we would have had to turn back so be cautious if bringing a pup. 10/10 worth the trek!
Big hike with elevation.  Take more water than normal.  Spectacular views.

Note, the parking here is limited and requires a park pass and a day pass (about $18 for three adults). This is a fantastic trail. We had fabulous weather! The trails are beautiful and take you by two lakes, a creek, some bridges, board walk, and beautiful forest colours at this time of year. It's definitely a challenging hike, especially for those without experience. My family has been hiking all our lives so we had no problems and really enjoyed the challenge of the crack rock scrambles and other. What's so nice about this hike is you get so many different topographies! Smooth rocks and quarts, the rock scrambles, earthy forest trails with rocks and roots, and the first part is a wide flat walk through a forest canopy. So much to see! I wouldn't necessarily say this is dog friendly unless your dog is an experienced hiker. I saw a few people take larger dogs up, and they were panting so loud you could hear them before seeing them. Please consider the weather and the climb on your dogs. Some people did not do the rock scrambles with their dogs. There's still fantastic views to see even if you don't go all the way to the peak. Personally, I took my Italian Greyhound (16 lb) up with absolutely no problem. He had a three point harness with a handle. He has been hiking since we adopted him. He is a better hiker than we are who can jump and climb and scramble up rocks with ease. But dogs with shorter legs, thick coats, etc. may not find it easy. I had to assist him over some larger crevices and rocks, especially on the way down, but overall we had an absolute blast!
Great trail but did not make it the last scramble to the top. My two year old lab was not up for it and too big for me to carry. Beautiful views along the way even without getting to the top.
Very hard to walk up the crack with a large dog, but it has been done! People are friendly, the views are amazing
Well marked trail, recommend getting there before sunrise to avoid crowds :)
Amazing views from the top; can get very crowded climbing up the crack; people leave too much toilet paper everywhere.
One of the best trails in Ontario

Arrived around 9:30am on Friday October 11. Maybe 7-8 parking spaces available not bad. Beautiful scenery. Fall colors popping. Clear and crisp conditions. Scrambling is my jam but take it slow and keep three points of contact, you’ll be fine! So much fun.

Great Views. Hiked The Crack at Sunset. If doing it for sunset ensure you bring proper lights for everyone (Headlamps) and warmer clothing. Hike back was in complete darkness for a large portion of the hike.
Slippery rocks after a a bit of rain
We left the trail head around 5am and got to the top to watch the beautiful sunrise! This is an extremely easy / low activity hike for a high reward.. our gps said we walked approx 9.01km

Wonderful picturesque views! The trail is moderate to complex depending on your shape and physique. For me as a short person, a couple of places very extremely difficult to climb, but manageable. Make sure to be wearing hiking shoes. The initial part is just a walk, then you face tree roots and stones, at the end there are rocks and steep rocks. Take your time and don’t hurry if you’re planning to make it to the top. :)
Excellent view, fun trail!
Very nice hike with a great view! Scramble through crack section is difficult but not very long. No bathrooms at parking lot seemed like a miss.

Well marked, well maintained trail. Gorgeous views and so worth the hike up! There is climbing involved so wear the proper attire and try to avoid coming when it has just rained/is raining since the rocks can be slippery! Dogs can hike the trail but there will be some parts where they might need to be hoisted/need help to climb up, especially if it is a smaller dog. Overall, I would highly recommend this trail - the most beautiful and well maintained trail I’ve ever hiked!
Excellente. Dry conditions, not too hot. Definitely recommend

Very challenging hike even for seasoned hikers. That being said the trail was full of hikers of various ages / skill levels moving at their own pace. 

re: “dog friendly” - while the trail may welcome dogs it is not entirely canine accessible or navigable. Do not attempt “the crack” section unless you are comfortable and confident scrambling large boulders solo-carrying your dog, or hiking with a partner able to assist.
The trail is a difficult trail. It has lot of climbing halfway through. But the view at the top is worth it. Takes atleast 4-5 hours  to finish the trail.
Trail rated moderate and for the most part it is. However, the last 200m involve hands and feet climbing over boulders
Some yellows and oranges. I think 19-20th Oct would be perfect for fall colors. The last 200 meters is hard especially on the way down. But you can still see views if you don’t go all the way up.

Multiple view points- plan for spending some time on the trail-you won’t want to leave the views!   

First half is lovely easy walk, nice little warm-up walk - can pick up pace here,  this portion is also a nice wide trail

Moderately challenging scramble to the top.  

Definitely goes to the top of my list for favourite trails in Ontario!
Amazing long hike with big slopes / elevations and boulders / rocks to climb. The top view is good but i personally liked the Chikanishing trail views a lot better and more beautiful !

Great trail that starts out easy and gradually gets more difficult as you reach the summit. The last km or so is basically rock climbing so bring grippy shoes or hiking boots. It's about a 3 hour hike walking at a leisurely pace. If you want to spend some time at the summit absorbing the spectacular views give yourself at least 3.5 to 4 hours to complete the journey. Trail is well marked, just follow the red markers all the way. Very nice half day adventure! Would highly recommend!
Easy
Great trail!

Great trail that’s well marked and maintained . The “crack” part would be challenging for young children and small dogs . Group of three active 30 yo’s and Australian Shepard managed to do it with included  15 mins break at top in around 2 hours 40 ish mins . Is closer to over 8 km. Beautiful view and definitely worth doing .
Fairly difficult hike due to elevation and terrain. The first half is mostly easy and flat and then it gets harder. Awesome views along the way and at the top!
hard
Can’t think of a better day hike in Ontario.

The last portion of the trail is a hard climb over large boulders so please wear sturdy hiking boots. We saw a few people wearing candles and I'm sure they must have turned around. The view at the top was amazing making it worth the challenge getting there!
What an amazing trail. Brought my golden retriever along, we took our time navigating the rocks, a very worth while experience. No issues going down, just again, took our time.
The last .7km is over only rocks and climbing. This is the most difficult part of the trail and not accessible to most folks looking for an easy walk or hike.
The last part is quite challenging. It’s more like bouldering than hiking.
Definitely a harder trail for beginners, has amazing views all the way up to the top. Definitely wear proper hiking shoes!!
Incredibly beautiful hike on a foggy day. The fog made the views come alive.
It was a bit slippery going up the rocks.   Even though it was cloudy the view was beautiful.
Always a delight!
Great trail and beautiful view at the top
Loved climbing the rocks.
Come early before the mass hoard. Too bad people can't keep their voices down, it destroys the experience.

This is more of an 8.5km. It was bug free but hot as hell (Sept 16th, 2024) when you start really ascending. It really is an "we must be there by now" till you get to the final daunting rock fall and think "oh, THIS  is what they're all talking about". It's a satisfying hike but you  need to mind the markers just as it starts getting steep. Bring lots of water, don't let anyone tell you that the rock fall isn't challenging...up and down...it's a feat. The views are stunning.  Take your time. Bring lots of water, wear good shoes, I brought a trekking pole that I stowed in my bag when I had to start using ARMS and legs to get to the top.   And the last marked 1km IS indeed the longest 1km...because it's 1.5km. I would mark this easy then moderate then hard. But a real trip. And yes, my distance says 9.3 BUT I will give the extra mileage  to time spent trying to find the markers in the middle. EYES OPEN, PEOPLE!!!

Been wanting to do this hike forever!! So worth it! It’s an easy hike up until the last maybe 200m that’s where it gets really steep and big rocks to climb! The part that made it difficult was hiking with our dog! He’s athletic however some of the climbs were too big for him to jump so we had to carry him which isn’t ideal when you are also trying to climb the rocks haha! Regardless SO FUN and the view from the top is unreal! Had a delish sandwich and went early enough that we had the lookout to ourselves!

The first 2/3’s of the trail is super easy walking… them there are a few ups and downs the final section through  “The Crack” is a scramble through rockfall. Gorgeous views from the top and nice spots to lay in The shade and have a snack and rest. To

Fantastic hike! Trail conditions were excellent. A bit of rain at the peak didn’t dampen spirits.

Take your time! This is a challenging hike.
Beauty trail, easier than expected.
I’m going with moderate. Easy hike until it isn’t but at 69 I pulled it off.
Beautiful but crowded in the summer
Very hard but worth it

Moderate hike with some boulder areas. Finished the hike in 2.25 hrs with a short break at the top. Able to complete it easily with an athletic shepherd. 
Parking fee was 18$
Awesome views! Fairly flat until the last half hour or so. You have to get a parking pass at the provincial park -  $18 for the day.
The view is always worth the climb!
Beautiful day on the trail. Should be fairly strong and agile to tolerate the last 1/3 of the work. We completed it in just over 3 hours with a small break at the top.

Amazing trail.  Made it into The Crack but encountered a maneuver at the boulders I couldn't get past ( and if I had, wouldn't have made it down from). Not disappointed though ..  amazing views and I accomplished everything I could.  Tough trail, but worth it.

Such a fun trail! Loved the varying terrain. We climbed on Sunday Sept 1 with dry conditions, 22°C, a really beautiful day. We got there about 10.30am and it wasn’t too busy but as we were heading back around 12.30pm there were quite a few groups on the way in. Took us 3.5 hours overall which included lunch at the top (15 mins rest)and a few photo stops.
The final phase of the climb just before the Crack is definitely a challenge but doable. I hiked it with my 2 dogs (1 yo and 2 yo cattle dogs) and they managed the climb with a little assistance. I would say if you’re bringing dogs make sure you can lift them. We had to use the handle on their harnesses to get across a couple boulders. 

A very beautiful, fun, well-marked, moderately challenging trail.

Rocky inclines that might make you go ‘should we turn around’ and plenty of ‘are we there yets’ if this is your first hike of the season. Wear grippy shoes as the rocks can be ankle breakers if you aren’t careful. Perfect weather conditions of a sunny day when we did the hike on labour day. Do not start the hike after 4 pm, it can be difficult to track the markers with low sunlight.

Rocky inclines that might make you go ‘should we turn around’ and plenty of ‘are we there yets’ if this is your first hike of the season. Wear grippy shoes as the rocks can be ankle breakers if you aren’t careful. Perfect weather conditions of a sunny day when we did the hike on labour day. Do not start the hike after 4 pm, it can be difficult to track the markers with low sunlight. It’s a 3 hour hike with sporadic water breaks and 10/12 minute snack break at the top.

Very nice trail, I agree with the trail being marked as a moderate/hard trail, as the climbing parts may not be suitable for all hikers. Regarding the dog friendliness, many people suggested it would not be possible/easy with a dog. In my opinion if your dog is agile and athletic with a taller build they should have no issues getting up the rocks. If your dog is not as athletic be prepared to have to carry them for some parts. Consider this risk before deciding to bring your dog with you.
Well labelled trail, it's a pretty hard trail very rocky and steep... need to be careful with footing but it's totally worth it at the top there is great views.. took me 3 hours

Very nice trail (The crack), I agree with the trail being marked as a moderate/hard trail, as the climbing parts may not be suitable for all hikers. Regarding the dog friendliness, if your dog is agile and athletic with a taller build they should have no issues getting up the rocks. If your dog is not as athletic be prepared to have to carry them for some parts. Consider this risk before deciding to bring your dog with you.
Took us 3.5 hours. First part is very easy. The scramble isn’t too bad. Views are incredible.

Spectacular views, Henvey Inlet windmills to the east,  Lonely Island to the south and Manitoulin to the west.  First ⅓ is an easy access trail,  next ⅓ moderate trail through deciduous orrest and the last ⅓ is a tough scramble up a rock fall.  The effort is well worth it.  Bring a chair and enjoy the view. Sturdy foot wear is an asset.
couple loose rocks on the climb but other than that. the trail was made longer because of a rotted part of the the forest but other than that amazing

Did this trail today, I would think if you have ever bought anything from MEC this trail won’t be as difficult as it’s states. Proper foot wear and lots of water if your going on a sunny day, it’s a hike, not a walk but we got to the top in an hour and a half with many stops because we are out of shape, tweaked my ankle like a rookie on the way back and had to basically limp back out like Quasimoto and still finished in 4 hours.  Bring a snack and sit at the top, it’s gorgeous.
THIS IS NOT AN EASY TRAIL!
Bring lots of water and a snack for the peak. Think ahead of bringing dogs it is dog friendly but be aware the conditions ahead as there is a lot of rocks to climb.
Starts easy but gets very challenging near the summit.

Beautiful trail! Mostly uphill on the way there with a scramble towards the end but worth the views! Walking at a moderate pace and making minimal stops it will take about 3-3.5 hours to complete if you're decently physically fit. Would not recommend taking dogs due to the scramble at the end.

This trail is definitely not hard. I would say moderate at most, easy if you’re an experienced hiker. There was one short section of incline. It was raining all day which made the rocks slippery and would be the only reason it was harder. Going slow between the cracks (especially if it’s slippery), is necessary.
Hiked the crack this afternoon, it was moderately difficult but the trail was in good shape despite the rain, it got pretty muddy as the rain intensified but was still worth the views

Well marked, busy trail. Use the bathrooms at George Lake campground, a 5 minute drive up the road as there are no facilities at the Crack Trailhead. We arrived by 8 on Saturday morning and not many cars in the small parking lot. Was quite busy by 10 or 11 am. Rocks are quite slick when wet so wear proper shoes.
Magnificent views from the top, making the boulder hopping on the way worthwhile
Climbing required which makes it so much fun. Be sure to have the right shoes. Binoculars are great to have up there too. Love this hike so much!
Some big climbs but well worth it!
Good trail, well marked, and well maintained. The last km or so is very steep climbing - would recommend shoes with a good grip
Well marked and such a rewarding view. Trail is in great condition!

This was an awesome adventure!  I didn't know what to expect - impossible to get lost and the varied terrain kept it very interesting!   The rocky part on the pack half was very cool and the look out at the top was amazing.  Highly recommend!!!
One of the best trails I’ve done!

My app didn't record well and it's actually closer to 9km with a detour. Incredibly difficult trail!  Be very prepared with lots of water! View is great!! Not for those with back problems or mobility challenges! There is a sign towards the end saying "1km till parking lot" and it's actually a lot closer to 1.5. Small washed out bridge section around the 2km mark.
It’s really just the last 1k that’s tough when you are on the scramble! Loved it and so glad we listened to the advice about solid footwear and water
Stunning

Absolutely incredible hike. It’s slightly longer than 6 km as they had to re-route part of the trail due to erosion. We added distance to our hike as we dropped something and had to back track approx. 1 km to get it. It was muddy in some sections and the bridge is washed out so your feet will get wet. HIGHLY recommend hiking boots as the scramble was quite difficult to navigate. Finding foot holes for both humans and dogs made the scramble slower than we originally anticipated.

One of my favourite hikes. Trail is now approx 8.5km and very wet and muddy during the first section. Bridge washed out so we took our boots off to cross. Make sure to have proper hiking footwear as the rock scramble requires good grip. Bring lots of water, bug spray and wear a hat on sunny days as the last section is quite exposed. Amazing views at the top and well worth the final climb!

great hike today. I was impressed with how well my dog did on the rocks. although she's a senior she very athletic. we had to lift her in a couple places. it was about to start raining when we got to the top so we didn't stay long so we could get back down the difficult section before it got too wet. Blueberries are in season right now!
Washed out bridge, but shallow water/ easy to get through. Challenging hike through the rock section but magnificent view at top.

My opinion and those of several other hikers was that the trail is nowhere near as hard as it’s made out to be on the provincial park website. The climb up through the Crack is over large rocks and requires caution — more on the way down than up. There were families with children, some looked as young as maybe 7ish. I’m sure small children with help from the adults will do just fine. The views were good (like most views from a high elevation are). Nothing spectacular. I went off trail and explored the ridge and found better views than from the main viewing area. Definitely a nice hike. This was early August so some mosquitoes in the lower wooded areas but no swarms. The parking pass also covers the Granite trail and a couple of others and you easily do all these in a day. Then head over the picturesque town of Killarney for Fish & Chips at Herbert’s!
New trail is a little longer.

such a fun hike! make sure you book your parking spot ahead of time as the wifi kinda sucks and you’ll need to show proof on your dash. also make sure that you have waterproof HIKING boots/shoes for this. no bugs for us, there is a scramble at the top, some sections were very wet and slippery, a bridge is broken where you have to walk through the water, and some of the muddy areas are quite deep. neither are deeper than your ankle but definitely something to consider. our mini aussie did quite well with the scramble at the top but we had to help him out at a couple spots. 10/10 would do it again if we find ourselves in the area!
Great trail. conditions were muddy and one of the bridges was flooded.  Bring bug spray.  The views are amazing at the top of the crack and the rock scramble at the end is a lot of fun.
There is one bridge washed out. We crossed barefoot then put our hiking shoes back on after we crossed. Lots of mosquitoes!

Absolutely gorgeous views, well worth the effort. First half is easy, lots of wet areas and bugs. One bridge is flooded, so need high waterproof boots or to remove footwear to cross. The rest of the trail is difficult with several areas of scrambling. Trail would be extremely slippery in the rain, wait for a dry day to do it. Take lots of water, you'll need it.  It is difficult but we are 63 and fit, able to make it to the lookout.
Buggy beginning, intense rain made the climb slippery and dangerous, and the trail was flooded most of the way. Nice view, but maybe skip it on rainy days.

Beautiful trail and views. We went Saturday, July 13, mid day. Beginning part of the trail was pretty buggy and muddy parts, but we had bug spray and were okay. hiking boots recommended. First foot bridge is slightly flooded. There are a number of areas with direct sun exposure for prolonged periods. We regretted not having hats and felt the effects of the sun - definitely recommend a proper head covering.
A little muddy!

Need reservations to park at the trail head unless you're camping at the campsite. Started just before 8 am and finished in under 4 hours with over an hour break at the top. We went off trail a bit on the way up and cut across the trail. climbed the boulder on the side as well that you see at the peak. There are now logs on the broken bridge, just need to balance over them. the first 2 km was pretty much flat. You get the elevation when you start scrambling. The mosquitoes were something else on this trail. Muddy in the beginning as well. Scrambling was fun and great views at the top. I would say this is a moderate hike
very muddy on the first section.

Lovely challenging walk with decent views at the top. 

Broken bridge with 1 ft of water meant we got wet feet at the start. 

Wear proper hiking shoes as you’ll need them for the scramble near the top. You’ll need to use both hands to climb! 

Bugs weren’t too bad - but we used plenty of deet.

Amazing views at the top. Difficult scramble, would recommend hiking shoes - you will need to use your hands to ascend at the end. Worth the effort with amazing views at the top. 

The bridge is currently broken and water was 1 foot deep when we crossed - so be prepared to get wet feet. 

Bugs are bad for the first 2km - use bug spray so you don’t get eaten alive! 

Enjoy!

The first third is a walk in the park, the back 2/3 are rocky and root prone and finally the scambling up the mountain. Half way there a partially submerged bridge and plenty of mud. I strongly suggest waterproof hiking boots with solid soles. The fabulous mountain top view is well worth the effort!
One of Ontario's top 5 trails. The trail currently is almost 9 km and 302 meters of  elevation gain.

I have done this hike in the past and it was great! Unfortunately when we were in Killarney recently we found out that you have to make a reservation in order to complete the hike. I’m not sure if this is new as I didn’t have to do this 4 years ago. It was a bummer as there was no space left and no park employee informed us about this when we registered or when my friends registered. There is a notification when they remind you about your campsite at the bottom of the email but I did not think to scroll down so that is on me. There is also no signage at the park informing people they need to register. This was one of the reasons we went to Killarney as well. So if you plan to do this hike I would recommend making a reservation in advance!
Busy but fun! Bugs aren't as bad now.

Bring hiking shoes/boots, water, and snacks. What others say about completing the trail with children and dogs is true, 80% of the rail is very easy, the last 20% is when it gets trickier with the rocks, It will be hard to get them to the top if you dont have proper gear. I carried my daughter with back hiking carrier, she is 18kg, plus the water and i was able to get to the top with no issues. Lots of mosquitos in early july, so be prepared for that as well. The view at the top is nice, but not the best ive seen in Ontario. Probably the view is better in fall.

The difficulty is way over rated. I’m 63 and moderately obese and had absolutely no issues in dry conditions. If it was wet, the rocks would be slippery but the distance was a bit understated according to my watch and iPhone and the elevation gain to the top is only 165m vs the 270 stated. There is a bit of up and down but nothing that got my heart rate going. The view is worth the 10k hike.   On June 27th the tree is still down across the beginning of the trail but no big deal.
Great view looking over the Georgian Bay. Lots of quartz. Just a great, not too challenging trail for anyone that can climb rocky uphills. If you hate mosquitos, go in August or even September.
Hard but gorgeous trail, scenic views from the mountain are really worth it!

I mean, it's the Crack. Best views in the area. A bit mucky and wet in spots due to recent downpour rainfall but most of it is easy to work around. What isn't is a downed tree that just fell today due to high winds near the start. I will try letting the park warden know as currently it's not easy to to work around.

First part of trail (approx 1.5km) is fairly easy. After the first bit the difficulty progresses very quickly. Good shoes definitely needed. Would not recommend doing the trail with small children or dogs unless very experienced. Climbing of rocks at some points is needed. Some areas where the rocks were wet, were quite slippery. 
Views are fantastic, bring lots of water, couple snacks and bug spray/net. Bear horn/spray or whistle recommended also for safety.

An absolutely wonderful payoff at the end of a challenging hike. Challenging but rewarding. Well marked. Clean. As others have mentioned first 2km or less were very buggy therefore the last two km are also buggy. This is mid June. A great in and out trail that I'd happily do again.
Hard but amazing
Trails in good condition - reservation for parking at trailhead required
First kilometre is full of bugs. Be extra prepared. Other than that the trail had marvellous views. We made noodles at the top. It was the time of this summer.

Lots of bugs for the first bit but once you hit the lake they aren’t that bad. Also, you can hike the crack with a toddler! Our son is 15months and loved being in the backpack. We also passed a lady with a two month old on the trail.

Trail is very filled with mosquitoes at the start/end. They clear up as you gain elevation, it’s still worth it, but we jogged quite a lot to avoid them. Our dog who is good with most rocks was too nervous for the craggy jagged rocks to make it to the very top. Very fun. Very buggy. Overall gorgeous and interesting hike.
Amazing view at the top! Completed the hike in 3 hours time. Lots of bugs the first 40 minutes. Dogs not recommended unless they are experienced.

Who hasn’t wanted to get right into the crack and maneuver your self through the challenging terrain? Amazing views and beautiful terrain on the way. You are required to check in at the park office to get a vehicle tag at no charge.
Great hike, gorgeous view at the top and along the way. Challenging near the end pretty easy for the majority!!
This time of year the bugs are bad till just after the bridge and then they mostly go away. Quite the elevation change so be prepared for that too. Not the easiest by any means.

Great trail! Well marked. Great views. There is a section of about 1 km (could be less, just felt like an eternity) that went through marsh and the mosquitos were horrendous. Our bug spray was no match.
It says dog friendly, which for the most part it is, but we definitely thought the end of the trail was not dog friendly. There were boulders that you’d have to climb to get up the crack and way too many crevices for potential paw injuries. Would do again though.

Would not recommend bringing a dog but the trail is great. Fair bit out of the way but the drive is worth it, especially if you’re camping just down the road. Gets fairly technical once you start ascending the rock face. Lots to explore slightly off trail to get a 360° view around the hill. Pretty tame for the most part, went with 1 person and we could talk throughout the hike.
Incredible trail, with great views. Took our dog with us and she had a blast. A bit difficult to get to the top with the dog but we made it!

Bugs are pretty bad at this time of the year, be prepared.
Amazing hike with good elevation and rock climbing.
Great challenge and lovely view at the top. The bugs were really bad and it was hot at the top. Don’t forget a hat!
Amazing views!! Bugs were pretty bad for us at the top. I dont recommend it for kids/dogs. Worth the challenge for sure!

i did it in just over 2 hours, if you are fit and an avid hiker its really not that challenging. the rocks near the top will slow you down but its not too bad. i did it with my dog, had to lift her up over some of the boulders to avoid her getting injured. trail was in perfect condition, no issues with bugs
Buggy, challenging, Rocky but worth the climb. Unreal view from the top!
Keep an eye out for bees when climbing the rocks . I almost put my hand in a group of them

Beautiful!
8.6km and 4 hours 
Was able to do it with my boxer dog but parts were difficult for him and myself. So worth the climb to the top!

Oh man, what a stellar view this was from the top! I'd say BC worthy how beautiful and high up you were! Lots of differing terrain as well! Scroll to the end to see the Northern Lights that night as well!
Wear good shoes and be ready to climb, amazing “hard” trail.  We took shortcuts in this hike so be ready to go the hard way.
A bit muddy but great walk arounds and  perfect weather
It’s hard on the rocks in some parts but it’s amazing otherwise
No bugs at this time of the year. Pretty challenging hike but it will be worth it once you reach at the crack.
Amazing crack trail, be ready to climb and have good shoes, water and food. It was wet today and the rocks a little slippery but worth every bit.

trail in excellent condition. far end of the bridge is still under water however water levels are down slightly so its a tad easier getting across from last year. staff tell me it's on the list of repairs for this year. Bears are out of hibernation so be cautious. I didn't see any on this adventure.

Honestly. It f#€kin rocks!! Go Do It. What are you waiting for? Put on your hikers and go do it!!

It’s wet w the thaw. Proper gear is always needed. But go do it!!!

@tbdadventures

#letsgetlost
Trail is clearly marked bring good hiking shoes and be prepared to push yourself at times.
Moderate difficulty, flat until the very end which requires a little climbing, great view and trail, not much snow and a little mud, overall 10/10
Still icy on the lower parts of the trail.  Beautiful day at the top with great views.
Good winter hike. Spikes mandatory, other than a few places being slippery, a very good place to visit in Winter.

Not sure why this is rated extremely difficult at the beginning of the trail.   I realize not everyone is fit but "difficult" could have been sufficient.    Enough snow to do it in snowshoes the whole way.  The best was going down the other side in untouched powder and return.  Double the distance and enjoy fresh powder

Little snow cover.
Crampons see definitely useful
Crampons work wonders and are needed for steeper parts of the hike. Trail was snow packed with some icy spots. Alot more rock showing this year. Snow is melting fast.

The Crack is exceptionally fun  
Harder than most hikes I've been on
Bring water and snacks

Great  trail, some part have snow some don’t 
We took 3hours 10minutes without break on the mountain top
The final part is super exciting and fun, be careful about covered crack, some are really dangerous when you can’t see them.
Probably now is the best day to visit without professional gear.

Easy to moderate till the crack, challenging and some bouldering required in the crack; great experience. It has nice views at the end . I think poles would be good to have. It took us 3 hours in total.

Awesome day on the trail. As expected it was muddy because it had snowed and melted day before. Barely anyone on the trail and had the top to ourselves. 
The first bridge is partly underwater. We were able to get around it by walking on logs and debris. I added pictures on my review. Some people said in review they had taken shoes off and walked across but I like my feet to stay warm, plus my shoes have gore-Tex. 
There wasn’t too much snow in the crack and was fine going up and down or. We were just more careful as it was wet and some snow in it. 
I had a great time hiking with my son!
First bridge is washed out. Bring boots or prepare to take off your socks. Lots of wet spots

Great views at the summit and plenty of fun scrambling!
Kakakise Bridge is partly submerged under the stream. Gradually sunk more between our first and second time using it, had to take off shoes and socks. Watch out for the current when crossing, water pretty cold!
2 weeks of rain, bridge was overflowing, but current was not overly strong and footing not slippery - took boots/socks off and crossed just fine, rest of the day was absolutely beauty
Awesome view, tough but fun rock climb.
Such a great hike! The climb was great, with some decent scrambling over rocks. Very well marked. The views at the end are incredible!
Muddy and wet, wear proper footwear for the scramble section. Overall great trail.

First time completing the crack and was as well maintained as can be expected. The water under the the bridge was starting to overflow onto the walk way but wasn’t an issue at the time I hiked. Perfect weather conditions cold but sunny and dry. Wouldn’t want to attempt this one in the rain!

Absolutely loved this trail. Once you hit the first lake, it's stunning spot after stunning spot. The climb up to and through the crack is easy too, so don't worry about it...the Ontario Parks site makes it sound a lot worse than it is. Just make sure you wear closed toe hiking shoes, bring plenty of water, and give yourself at least 6 hours, since you'll be stopping and taking photos all along the route. The viewpoint at the top is also a perfect lunch stop spot.
Very hard. We definitely underestimated this trail, lots of climbing and steep rocks. Knees are destroyed but the views were 100% worth it. Also, dont forget to register for parking!

First 2/3 is easy to moderate forest walk with some rocks and roots. Once you get to the rocks it’s a bit of a climb, but very doable if you’re in appropriate footwear; hiking boots or something with ankle support is a must. Going down the rocky part is much more challenging than going up. If you’re unsure about your balance or comfort with scrambles, hiking poles might be a good idea. The re-route in place does add 600 m (though not particularly demanding) to the route so keep that in mind when expending your energy.  Overall a fun and moderately difficult trail. Probably risky if it’s wet or raining as the rocks do get very slippery.

I was nervous heading into the hike because of the reviews about scrambling etc. But it was not bad at all! The scrambling made it fun. We went while it was raining so definitely a bit more slippery. Wear good hiking shoes. I would rate it as moderate. The first 3km is like a nice walk in the forest. The scrambling isn't tough, but can be daunting when looking at it. The way down is harder.
Slippery after rainfall, need permit to park (can get online or at gatehouse)

Tough and challenging 
But it was wet windy and extremely cold. When we got to the top there was sleet, and it was windy and freezing. 
But worth all the effort. 
The views were amazing. 
If you’re fit then it’s a must do, but beware you have to climb most parts with your hands and feet!
Didn't have time go the whole way, so just to the second point
Amazing. Proper shoes and willingness to grab some rocks will make this a proper proper climb. I wish I brought my chalk lol. Lots of opportunity to climb your own way. Amazing. Just being boots.
Wear hiking boots, slippery in the rain

The beginning is a warm up. Then the 2/3 portion gets more intense. Then the last third is a good scramble using well placed footwork and hands for leverage. The rest and vista view at the top will be well deserved and worth it all…. but also rewarding views along the way too. Be careful on the way down! 

The detour portion of the trail lengthens it a bit, but it’s a lovely scenic detour along the lake, and a more gradual incline through the forest.

Being well into October it was all mostly dry and no bug free!
Great trail. Good path beautiful views
The crack trail took me about an hour to go to the top. I continued on the blue trail, there are several beautiful lookouts for the next two km.

Unmatched views and the rock scramble to the top makes this trail uniquely challenging. Overall not the most interesting trial until the last kilometre or two but for what it lacks the views make up for. Took us just under an hour to get to the top.

The trail itself is great. We hiked it on September 30th under great weather condition so not slippery. Only the last about 1/4 was quite difficult while the beginning was easy. Great view of the Killarney fall color. On the other note, the road of Killarney was quite disappointing, unpaved and rough plus people drove fast, making it very dusty.

This is one of my favourite Ontario trails! It's mostly flat, but there is some bouldering involved, as well as walking over rocks that get slippery when it's raining. In bad weather, it may be useful to bring hiking poles. 

The view at the top would be worth it even if the trek up was much more technical than it is!!
Trails great, dry and well marked. Pretty busy but expected on a beautiful Saturday. Water still warm in the lake, my girl went for a dip! We and most everyone got a ticket for not buying a park pass
Nice hike but prepared to walk through the rocks at the last 1 km.
Beautiful trail beautiful hike. Make sure you're wearing great trail or hiking shoes and enjoy the view!

Detour makes it 8.5km in and out. . Easy hike for first 3rd, slight climb for 2nd third and last third is a climb /scramble across rocks and boulders. Well marked for most but less so at top so you have to figure path out on your own. Need good hiking shoes and great mobility and balance.  Wouldn't tackle  this if wet as it would be slippery down. Took us 3 hrs and we added another half hour at top to soak it in. Highly recommended if you're comfortable climbing rocks. One of our favourite hikes for the workout and the views.
No bugs. Super dry. Trail is well marked once you get to the rocks. There is a boulder section that is difficult if you have dogs with you. Just need to take it slow. Beautiful view from the top!
Absolutely wonderfull
The views at the top of the ridge are every bit as good as people say they are.  Enjoy! :)
Absolutely amazing
great views for effort
No bugs or mud this weekend! Absolutely gorgeous
It was perfect weather for us, clearly marked trail. It was busy this weekend. The trail was very difficult, bring good shoes and enjoy the views from the top.
Easy to start. The last kilometer is climbing up some big boulders.
Beautiful view at the top of the crack. Take lots of water and snacks as it is a difficult hike at the last leg, and nice to the a break at the look out. Sturdy hiking shoes is a must.
Moderate trail, great view. Would not recommend for dogs.
Excellent and challenging trail with incomparable lookout. Going to the summit will take you over a rock slide and beautiful white cliffs.
Worth the challenge! The steep climb at the top was not as bad as we expected. We continued past the main lookout on the blue trail a bit for some additional views.

This was a fantastic day to hike the crack. We went a little later in the morning than we'd like (10:30 am), however, we found fairly minimal crowding and no bugs! The hike up was peaceful and pleasant and we had no real trouble traversing even the hardest parts. 

As other reviewers had already mentioned, the first half to three-quarters of the hike is very easy and quite pleasant. As you reach the end, the hike gets significantly more difficult with the final section requiring scrambling and careful foot placement. Please ensure that if you are hiking when it's wet, the rock surfaces can be very slippery. Be sure to have good sun shade as you will be exposed to the elements  near the end as well. Signage is pretty clear and we never really had to consult our maps or phones to check where we were.

Amazing trail. Challenging one especially when coming down the top. Make sure to wear hiking boots as there are points rocks throughout the trail and parts of it requires good grip. Breathtaking view from the top

Perfect day for this hike! Starts out going a few km through flat ish double wide trail then you cross a bridge and enter some rooty/rocky trail running beside the lake.
