You start uphill for a bit before reaching some large flat rocks that lead to the crack.  The crack itself is a great choose your own adventure style rock climbing past large boulders.  The views at the top are panoramic and amazing.  Enjoyed conversation with other hikers and my apple before heading back.  Took a little over 3 hrs. Wouldn't recommend in wet weather as the rocks would be very slippery on the way down.
Good conditions, not a lot of bugs. Lots of climbing rocks, definitely not for a casual stroll but worth the view
Great but challenging trail. Detour made it 8.5km. Took me 2.5 hours.
Great trail, fun for experienced hikers, our 7yr old girls did great! Recommend being physically mobile for rock scrambles

First couple kilometres are flat on a wide trail through the forest but the scenery ramps up considerably from there. First through a lovely pine forest along the shore of Kakakise Lake then up the quartzite hills until you reach the crack itslef. Insipiring views of lake killarney and the west from the top. Took 4h40m with an 8 and 4 year. Kids really loved the climb to the top.

Well marked trail with a fun climb/rock scramble to the top.  
Great views all the way to Tobermory on a clear day.
Easy scramble at the end, lovely views all around!
Amazing trail
We are out of shape middle Agers, we did the hike with detour in 3hrs with a break at the top. The rock climbing can be tough but so glad we conquered it!

Challenging trail, at least the boulders part. It is 9.3 km, they've set up a detour for a portion in the forest, which makes it a bit longer. 
Did it with a bit of drizzle, wasn't busy at all. A booking is needed and in normal conditions the trail gets busy (so I have been told by the park ranger).
The view from up there is breathtaking, worth the climb. Good boots needed, though I saw a chick with rubber boots on the forest.
The views at the peak are stupendous however good hiking footwear is a must. Overall an excellent, well marked trail.

You need to pay to enter the park. Gate house is a 8km drive past the trail open, with no signs at trail open to notify you of this. They only sell a limited amount of tickets - so you're SOL if you get there too late.
Did it with my 7 and 10 year old, would t try it with any younger kids. Wasn’t too buggy but the climb near the top was right on the edge of my 7 year olds comfort zone. They both loved it tho!
This is a challenging trail but worth it if you feel comfortable climbing up and down tall rocks.

Awesome trail. Buggy for the first bit, but then a beautiful climb through white quartz, plus a fun scramble. Short and sweet.

The scramble is definitely doable by small kids, our 8yo and 5yo were able to complete on their own.

Poles aren’t very useful. It’s not quite steep enough on the hike, and they get in the way on the scramble.
Gorgeous and worth all the hype. Dynamic with fun switch backs from the updated route. Bring proper hike footwear with grip. Take your time scrambling and scaling the rocks. So fun!
Amazing views and wonderful rock and features
Really good trail. Worth the 2.5 hour hike for the view alone. Shaded by trees for the most part which helps keep the temperature in check. 5/5

Great trail for a good long hike. Multiple reviews said the first half was very buggy; sprayed bug repellent prior to walk and was fine. Hiking boots or shoes recommended as trail is very rocky. I recommend bringing a lunch and snacks as well as two water bottles; it’s worth staying a while at the top and having a picnic while soaking up the views. Decent can be a little tricky especially closer to the top; if it rained, rocks are slippery. I started my hike around 10h30; there were not many people; once at the top, around 11h45, there were 4 other people. After 12h30, the trail becomes really busy.
Amazing views and a challenging hike.
Solid hand over feet rock scramble for 1.5 mile to the top. Great views!
beautiful! easyish start and then really nice and technical climb through the rocks. down was harder than up IMO. view was amazing, even on super overcast day.

Depending on your hiking fitness level, I would classify this as a difficult hike. The first portion of it is simple on flat land on a very wide path, but then it gets a little steeper until finally you are rock climbing up the sides of the rocks to get to the lookout point. Definitely a rewarding but challenging hike. Hiking shoes or good gripped runners are a must. Saw so many people going in on our way out wearing sandals and flip flops… definitely would not recommend that & is not a great choice. Bring lots of water, it can get hot in the sections when you’re climbing the rocks. View at the top is worth it.
Difficult, but amazing.
Long first stretch with bugs but the top is rocky and beautiful  went with the doggo
Freaking amazing!!!

After spending a year in BC I was so happy to do a mountain-style hike. Trail was well marked- just follow the red markers. Definitely a challenge towards the end to get to the top (and to get back down) especially with a dog. My dog is medium sized and she did well, but was quite exhausted afterwards! I suggest using a retractable leash for the scramble section. It truly was such a beautiful view at the top- a little bit smoky but stunning nonetheless. Definitely bring lots of water and snacks to enjoy with the view :)

Definitely need good hiking footwear for this one. The first 1.7 km is flat and wide. It then gets more interesting and at 2.8 km there’s an elevation increase.  The final section is a lot of fun and somewhat 
challenging as you scramble up the rocks and through the crack. The views from the top is fabulous and fortunately unencumbered by the wild fire smoke today. Bonus: the blueberries are starting to ripen, so fresh fruit snacks are available for the picking.

Amazing hike/ climb. Highly recommended. Various sections, was able to bring my medium sized dog up to the start of the crack,but she was unable to continue. Beautiful view, but very smoky due to forest fires.
First part is easy with well marked trails in woodsy area. The last part is scrambling and you need to be careful. The view is beautiful but could use better markers at the top.

First 1.5 really is mosquito alley. Then you think it’s not too bad. Then you scramble the entire last bit which is a fun challenge. App cut off half way though took around 2 hr 40 mins to do 8.25 kms.

Beautiful trail definitely worth it! Someone else mentioned everything I wanted to say so I’ll just summarize it.
1.) pee before you get there, there’s no bathroom anywhere on the trail 
2.) there’s bugs the entire way up bring your bug spray with you you’ll sweat it off 
3.) we bought our permit online, the wardens can use an app to check the license so as long as it’s the car you registered with there’s no need to display a permit.
4.) the first 2 k are easy peasy after that there’s some incline, roots, rocks if you have weak ankles be careful. The last km is climbing, technical watch your foot work.  Now, I’m moderately fit , kinda chubby but I get by with most active things and I didn’t have too much trouble so don’t believe all the reviews I feel like most people can do this as long as you’re not battling weak ankles or maybe severe asthma there’s a few huffy puffy parts
5.) yes. The view is worth it.

Amazing hike with fantastic views! We went midday, took us about 2 hours 45 minutes + an additional 45 minutes to take in the view/take photos at the top. Very buggy from beginning to end, bring bug spray! We are in moderate shape and didn’t find the trail strenuous, just challenging and technical (slippery and tricky in areas) during the last 500 metres or so to the top. We bought our parking permit online, no need to display it despite an old sign saying it was necessary to do so. There are no washrooms at the trailhead - closest facilities are at the Killarney gatehouse if you continue a few kilometres up the road. Parking lot is small but we went on a Tuesday around 1 pm and had no issues at all. Loved the trail, it’s now one of our favourites.
Fairly buggy but as people have said the trail is easy the first 3/4 but more of a challenge the last 1/4. The view is completely worth it.
Easy hike early on. The last 1/3 is a bit hard, requiring some scrambling. We went on 11th of June - sky was cloudy and there were some mosquitoes.
1st half was straight forward. 2nd half a bit challenging with the rocks but amazing view at the top

A  bit buggy (to be expected for June), but thankfully, we had a breeze to help keep them away. The first 3/4 of the trail is easy. The last half you are climbing over rocks. We managed to get to the crack in 1.5 hrs. It was a little hazy from the fires but cleared by the end of the day from the wind.
Relatively easy
Lovely trail - hard and very buggy so be prepared!

Great trail with rewarding views! Definitely a moderate/hard route if you’re not experienced enough. I’d recommend some face nets or heavy duty bug spray, the black flies were of the masses. Really enjoyable hike with some climbing! Be safe out there!
Bad mosquitos!!!
Is a tough trail not for the casual hiker
Too many black flies, garden snakes
Great hike, views at the end are spectacular. First 2/3 would be fine for dogs. Last 1/3 would be challenging for any dog that isn’t part mountain goat.
Great hike at the crack, good views on top of a peak. The hike back to the park was beautiful but long.

Trail markers are poorly done. Without this app I would have been lost. There are gorgeous views on the way up but getting through the actual crack is a climb over large boulders. I'm in very good shape for my age but couldn't complete the trail for the view.
Very fun trail, might want to have some experience and good footwear. Very good views.

Well marked trial. Make sure to carry bug spray! Else you will get swarmed with them. It’s a big nuisance especially when you are climbing the tricky rock sections on top. Other than the bugs, the trail is good with a beautiful view at the top! Worth the hike

Went in September 2019. Loved this trail. Spectacular view with the fall colors. The first half is very easy, but the difficulty increases with the second half - some scrambling and very minor climbing required. Start early (the parking lot fills up quickly on weekends) and ensure you have time to savor the view at the top. A must do hike in Ontario! Note: be careful in poor weather, rocks are very slippery.
2nd time with the kids, 7 and 3. Did it a bit faster this time but the bugs were pretty annoying. Glad we brought big jackets.
Breathtaking views from the final lookout.

I would give this trail more than 5 stars if I could.  It was spectacular.   Trail is well marked and maintained.  After a week with no rain, there were a couple of muddy spots but nothing really.  Most of the trail I would rate as easy to moderate…gentle grades but with rocks and roots to tangle up your feet sometimes.  The scramble to the top is tricky, so would rate that part more challenging.   As long as you are in reasonably decent shape with good solid hiking boots/shoes it is absolutely do-able.  Just be careful and take tour time if you are unsure.  We loved it - will be back another time to do it again!

Great hike.
Quite easy for the first 4 km.  The last few hundred meters (the actual « Crack » where the trail takes its name) consist of large boulders that need to be climb over.  This is the part that makes this trail difficult.  Going down is as challenging.
Well marked Trail easy hiking until the end then a moderate to difficult scramble to the top.
Great trail, didn’t find it too difficult to hike with dogs. Some muddy and buggy spots but over all was a great trail!

This trail was…challenging.  It was also absolutely worth the view.  A little mushy in places, but not too bad.  Leave yourself lots of time; Personally wouldn’t want to come back in the dark.  Gorgeous trail and spectacular views.
Great trail for experienced hikers
Bit of a tough climb but 100% worth it!!! An absolute must do!!

Hiked the Crack on May 6, 2023. Some muddy parts but they were avoidable by taking the bush slightly. One of the bridges had a small section under water. Some people walked across on a small log but we decided to take off our shoes/socks and walk through it. The rocks at the top are dry and in good condition. It took us about 2 hours with 4 dogs and a few water breaks for the pups! Overall it’s a great hike.

It is my 2nd time hiking on this trail and I will never be tired of viewing incredible  sceneries along it. Will rate the difficulty: intermediate to hard, reason being its muddy and slippery ground, rocky cracks, water bridge and length. It is definitely worth of trying.
Good luck on your trail walk some time
Very muddy at parts, but rocks going up to the top very dry not slippery
Some wet spots and slippery rocks but trail is in surprisingly good shape

Very icy so don't go there with sneakers.
The path is a bit messed up so be willing to go around obstacles (meaning sometimes getting your feet wet). It can get slippery when melting. Wouldn't recommend for small children.
It's worth it for the final view! Took us 6h to complete today going very casually and doing some break every hour.
Well-mainted  trail with clear marking signs. Come before 11AM definitely avoid crowed parking spot.
Excellent trail given the winter conditions!

went there yesterday and there was around 4 feet of snow when climbing to the crack. i recommend wearing ice cleats on your hiking boots if you’re going to the top. trail will take you about 4 hours round trip unless you’re a pro :)
Just hiked it this weekend. Quite a bit of snow but packed down. Rocks were slippery but doable. Coming down was a lot of sliding ..
Just hiked it this weekend. Quite a bit of snow but packed down. Rocks were slippery but doable. Coming down was a lot of sliding ..

Great hike with a wonderful viewpoint at the top! Went around midday and only ran into some folks on the trail when we were hiking back down.

At one point, the trail goes over a bridge/beaver dam — if you're not wearing waterproof boots, your feet will get soggy.

The rocks/scramble near the top could be challenging if you have mobility concerns (or young kids!). Overall, lots of fun and I definitely recommend it!

It took us 2 hours 40 minutes, including a lunch break at the top.

Snow was washed away so we tackled this in December. As long as you have good hiking boots, you’ll be fine. Definitely muddy and the rocks leading up to the Crack and in the crack were quite slippery. 

Awesome hike up and you just need to be careful on the way down so you don’t slip. Scenic, peaceful, no one else on the trail. Even on a gray day it was a terrific hike and view.

Like other trekkers, we’d agree it’s more than 2 hours. We were just under 3 hours with a stop at the top for a snack and the view.

Fantastic trail with spectacular scenery and views. The could be a bit tricky if mobility is an issue. Watch for slippery rocks when wet. Give yourself enough time to take in the views and check out the cool geology.
Refreshing no one else on the trail so peaceful

Hiked this trail about a month ago and I can say so far this is the most fun trail, in Ontario, that I’ve hikea so far. Wouldn’t say it’s difficult if you’re an experienced hiker and/or if you have done hikes with elevation out west but definitely not easy towards the end. 
- Waterproof shoes are a must. Do not hike this trail with hiking sandals
- 3/4 of the trail is easy and 1/4 is where it gets fun and challenging. You might have to use all your hands and legs to jump over all the rocks. Super fun
- Even if you’re experienced, give yourself 3 hours or more because the picturesque views will make you want to stay when you reach the top
- There are red and blue markers. Please follow the red markers to stay on the crack. I believe the blue marker takes you on a 80 km back country trail. So, if you didn’t come for a back country expedition, red markers are for this specific trail

Photos really don't convey how beautiful this trail is, even in the off season. Photos also don't convey how much of a scramble the crack portion is, definitely not a beginner trail (easily the hardest one I've done in Ontario) and hiking shoes are a must.
The end of the bridge at the beginning was submerged but thankfully we had waterproof shoes so it wasn't too bad to cross. Portions were definitely very muddy and wet but not enough to take away from our enjoyment of the trail.
Lots of scrambling but sooo much fun

Amazing view and super cool landscape throughout. The first half of the trail is a simple hike through forest while the second half is a steep incline up rock. As a moderate hiker I didn’t find the hike too laborious but definitely tricky to navigate

Great trail! We're casual hikers and were able to complete it in about 3 hours. A little difficult towards the top, but not impossible. Absolutely recommend boots or good hiking shoes. We brought our dogs, and they did make it up with a little help. I would recommend a harness that you can lift your dog with if you have a bigger dog. Overall very fun!

Unfortunately very foggy today, but still a nice hike with a bit of scramble towards the end. Trail was muddy at parts, the bridge is semi submerged, rocks slick, but trail is still in good condition, would recommend boots. Moderate rating is appropriate.
Good shape and wide, steep and Rocky climb at the end

One of the most fun hikes you can do in Ontario! It's not really difficult per say, especially if you've been out west, but you should be at least a little bit experienced as a hiker because you will be expected to do a bit of rock scrambling near the top. That's the best part! Views are always great up top, but after all the recent rain the base level is pretty muddy and mucky. Bring hiking boots and gloves, especially if it's wet.
Wow
Detour of 600m due to erosion.
Well maintained, a little route finding required towards top. Took us 1h40 travel time round trip
Re route in effect due to erosion. Great trail.

3/4 is trail walking = easy then rest is bouldering = moderate (glad I didn’t bring my dog) Booked $15 parking permit online - no printing required. Didn’t get busy until around 11am.  Hiking boots/shoes suggested (seem some crocks and they couldn’t make it lol)

2/3 of the hike is easy with wide forrest paths & some nice lake views on the way. The last 1/3 is rock climbing and tough in spots. You need proper hiking boots. The view is magnificent once arrived. The distance indicated on this app doesn’t make sense - we recorded 3.4 miles instead of 4.5.
What a hike! Dont be fooled by how easy it is at first… the last bit it technically challenging with scramble and big rocks. The views are totally worth it! Definitely a busy spot, so come early!
Amazing hike. Climb is soooo worth the views.

 3/4, then it climbs and you scramble for the last bit up through "the crack".

You’ll be feeling it in the legs and you’ll likely be huffing and puffing towards the end of the trail, but you can do it! And you will feel such a sense of accomplishment when you get to the top knowing that this is said to be one of the more difficult hikes in Ontario :) 

I did it without any ice cleats or crampons, simply because I don’t have any, I would’ve if I did lol, but if you like me don’t have any, you will be fine in some boots with good traction, there are some icy parts later on in the trail when you start the ascent to the crack, but I found that there is always a way around them, and they’re fun to slide down on your way back :)

The trail is well marked and well walked, you won’t have a hard time finding your way :) 

When you get to the crack at the end of the trail, the gaps between the boulders are filled with snow, making it much easier to get up them than it would be in the summer time I imagine, if you’re thinking about going and doing it but are unsure if you’re able to, just go and send it :) I believe in ya :) give yourself at least 4 hours of daylight, bring 2L of water or so, some food to eat when you reach the top, and you’ll be all good :) I reached the top in an hour and 10 minutes, spent about an hour on the top of the ‘mountain’, and it took me an hour and a half to get back, but I was cooking it. I could see it taking 2 hours both ways if you are casually walking and taking everything in.

Make sure you have enough gas too! The closest gas station I found was about 45-50 minutes away in Sudbury, I almost ran out of gas lol :) You’ll find the trail head about 7km ahead of the main office, you’ll see a sign for it. The pay-for-parking machine at the trail head only takes credit, if you don’t have a credit card you can get a ticket at the main office

Despite reading lots of reviews and posts about this trail, it was still somehow harder than I was expecting, and I'm an experienced hiker. 

The first 1-2k is an easy, flat trail through the woods, which can get a little muddy, but it was fine. 
Once you get past the bridge and to the re-route, it gets a little trickier and a little muddier, but still fine. There are also some gorgeous lakes at this point. 
Then, once you get over the first quartzite hill, it really starts getting tricky, but the scenery is fantastic and you feel so isolated from the world at that point. You will have to do some hands & knees climbing at this point too. 



The very last bit, once you've gotten to the top of the mountain, which I think is the part that's called 'The Crack' is the hardest bit of hiking I've ever done. It wasn't even hiking, it was literally rock climbing. I really wasn't sure I was going to be able to do it - and I'm young and able-bodied. I mustered up the courage and climbed up on my hands and knees. It was well worth it though, as the views on top are fantastic. I had to pretty much slide and jump down the rocks on the way back down. 

Some of the reviews make it seem like it’s all easy until you get to ‘The Crack’ and then it’s clambering up the boulders, but basically the entire ascent up the mountain is hard and The Crack is even harder. 

We went in mid-November at 8am, and we only saw three groups of people as were doing the return trip. I can't imagine trying to do some of the trickier climbing bits with a bunch of people watching and waiting. Some points of the hike are also on the cliff-side and quite precarious, so it would be very tricky to do if it was busy. 

Also, the AllTrails stats and signs posted on the trail are very misleading. It took me just over 9km and just over 5 hours (lots of time to admire the views). 

The trail was also surprisingly poorly marked, for such a popular trail. If you’re not paying attention, it would be very easy to get lost. There were points where I thought I had completely lost the trail, but if I looked around, there would be a tiny blaze somewhere off in the distance.

Despite how hard it was, I'm already craving a return trip. I highly highly recommend every hiker in Ontario take a crack at 'The Crack'  at least once.

Once you can see the rock wall it begins to change to moderate-challenging. Some areas of rock are not bad to climb and other areas felt like I was scaling a rock wall without support (mind you I'm not a fan of heights and I have a general fear of falling).
Climbing in The Crack itself is very narrow and steep. There is enough grip available on the rocks to climb but it could take longer... be patient with yourself!
Once you get to the top you will enjoy spectacular views of other mountains and  some small lakes. Sit and savour the moment... and then turn around! Do not keep going or you will follow La Cloche trail and that is very very long, unless you're prepared and want to do it. We were confused and kept following the trail markers for another 2km until we turned around. The hike was around 15km for us.
I would love to do this again as The Crack gives a beautiful view, but I was not into the rock climbing. La Cloche on the other hand I would definitely like to tackle one day!
Ps: I recommend you go early. We arrived at 730am. By 1130am there were crowds, families young and old, and it would have been irritating to navigate through everyone and wait behind inexperienced groups. Some folks had hiking sticks for the beginning of the trail but you cannot use these for the climb itself.

The view from the top is amazing. One of the best views I've seen in Ontario. This is also one of the most difficult hikes in Ontario due to the steep incline and the need to climb over boulders but it's still accessible to anyone in good physical condition. However, proper hiking shoes would also go an extremely long way. 

The hike is not 7.2 kilometres, as AllTrails lists it as. It's closer to 8.5-9 roundtrip. Based on their number, I mistakenly thought the peak was by the 3.5 kilometre mark but, in reality, that was just after the first set of boulders. There is currently a detour around the main trail due to maintenance, which would account for the discrepancy.

As other reviewers have mentioned, the first 3 kilometres are flat. The last 1.5 or so is on an incline and require some climbing. You will likely have to use your hands so I would recommend you bring some gloves. We went in mid-October when the high was 7 Celsius and it was perfect for the hike. It did rain the night before but this didn't affect the route much. However, it also rained again shortly after we reached the summit and that made conditions on the way down slippery, so dry conditions would help. The route is mostly shaded but the later sections are open so keep that in mind if you're going during the summer. Personally I would not recommend doing this trail in hot weather. 

In terms of the difficult portion at the end, there are sections with boulders followed by flat ground, so you'll always have spots where you can catch your breath, if you need them. The boulders are also well trodden, so you never have to think too hard about the best way up. I can see the climb being made way more difficult when it's crowded. My suggestion would be to leave early. We got there later than we planned, about 9:30am on a Saturday, and the parking lot was almost full. Traffic on the route wasn't an issue. By the time we turned around, we ran into some congestion while descending. At 2:30pm, as we were leaving, cars were parked all up and down the main road and people who drove in from Toronto were just starting. Keep in mind there is a 14 dollar charge for parking. I have no idea whether the people who parked on the street also paid for parking.

Obviously, pack a bag with water and snacks. It took us five hours total, including photos at the top, but I can see it taking longer for others. There are also no washrooms anywhere on the trail, including by the parking lot.

In the end, this was one of the best trails I've done. We're already planning another trip back next year. Good luck!

Beautiful trail! We went on a rainy day so it was slightly muddy and slippery. Markers were confusing at one point because parts of the trail have been rerouted, but we found our way back!
Got rained out - had another 350m to go but rocks were too slippery making it unsafe. Beautiful views and a great hike regardless of the rains.
Awesome trek!!  Good scramble at the top.  Fantastic views and scenery!!
Was great trail should be rated difficult for at the end lots of climbing rocks. Beautiful views at the end.
Very busy on a Saturday. Narrow parts with people going in both directions not ideal during Covid. Hike was enjoyable and technically challenging towards the end.

amazing trail. don't let the first bit fool you!
wear proper shoes with support if you plan on going to the top for the best view ! 
stay safe.
Busy Saturday trail- not covid ideal. Technically challenging at parts.
Awesome trail! Great views.
I would call it more like easy-moderate trail. Beautiful views from the top. Very busy in the weekends.
I would call this difficult instead of moderate because of the final stretch. You have to scramble over a bunch of rocks. This would not be easy for anyone who is not in good physical shape.
100% worth it. first km is a little boring but the rest quickly makes up for it. a bit of scrambling on the rocks but nothing too steep. spectacular views.
This place lives up to its reputation. Once to the top and the vista viewed it’s almost a feeling of enlightenment. Slippy if wet prepare to do some crawling and intense rambbling

We hiked up for sunrise! It was a beautiful view and we had the viewing point all to ourselves. Hiking up in the dark was a little difficult, but an experienced hiker with poles and a headlamp should be fine. Took us 1.5 hours to get up and 1.5 hours to get down. Would definitely hike this again.

Lovely hike. Busy but rarely felt crowded. Lots of other hikers at the top, but there is lots of space to enjoy an unobstructed view. Agree with other reviews: wear good footwear, it gets harder, lots of nice views all along the route, would be slippery in wet conditions. Climbing up the narrow "crack" was fun.
Awesome hike with awesome buds

The first km is pretty dull, but afterwards it morphs into some nice easy switchbacks before the gentle rock ascent and scramble. views are totally worth it. I did it with a 10 yr old husky and was amazed by how well he did on the boulder scramble. 

Would absolutely recommend!
Awesome scramble near the top! Gorgeous views
sooth start than after gets technical while climbing up .... climbing big rocks  view is amazing!

One of the best hikes you can do! The hike itself is fun/interesting/challenging and the views at the top are awesome! Luckily no bugs at all when we were there on a sunny day. Leaves were just starting to turn colour. Trekking poles may be helpful esp coming down. You will need to use your hands to help in some sections but just take your time. If it’s wet out, rocks will be slippery and is not recommended. Parking lot was full and lots of cars had to park along the road but didn’t seem to be a problem. There’s a pay station in the parking lot by the trailhead if you don’t have a parking pass already. The trail is 7km east of George Lake campground/main entrance (could get a pass there/refill water bottles if you forgot/use bathroom). Bring a mask to go inside!

Trail is long, tiring, hard on the ankles and knees. Wear good hiking shoes because the trail is very rocky and steep at the end. Markings are clear. DO NOT attempt in the rain, the trail is already slippery in parts on a sunny, dry day. Trailhead information board says 6km but my watch recorded almost 9km so be aware. Took about 3.5 hours round trip with 45 minutes stopping at the top.
Amazing! Climbing rocks made my day. Hell, made my month. One of the best trails I've ever done and you will ever do.
Wear running shoe/trail runner with rubber bottom to absorb shock, current generation of foam bottom runners are terrible at handling rocks.
Beautiful but a difficult trail. Such a variety of natural vistas- woods, lakes, rocks, 360 degree views. Excellent footwear is a must. Stay hydrated.

It costs $15.50 for a day pass now. We were lucky to hike it on a windy day, so no bugs thankfully, other than hornets flying all over the place. We got there around 10:20am and got to the highest point at 11:40am, hung out for a bit then headed back. There are some areas of trail that have been blocked off and rerouted so there's a little bit of confusion when climbing back down from the top to the forest trail area. Other than that, it wasn't the most difficult hike. Definitely tiring but not too crazy. Make sure you bring enough water, and snacks. We didn't bring enough water so we felt like we were going to die on our way back down. Learn from our mistake!
Amazing views! The rocky parts are challenging but it makes the trail very fun — wouldn’t want to go after rain because it would be quite slippery! Amazing views.

Great hike, beginning is pretty easy, then some quality uphill and light scrambling towards the summit, lots of areas exposed to the sun, trail is quite busy and pretty well marked. Bugs weren't too bad at all. Super fun, took about 4 hours all in all
The canoe to trail option was swamped in and we had to bushwhack to get to the trail. Trail itself is challenging and spectacular.

Amazing trail .. we did it with a 2 year old and a one year old. It got tough in between, especially towards the end where you have a climb up the slope. It took us around 4.5hours because we had to make multiple stops for the kids. 

Wouldn’t recommend the trail on a rainy weather as it may get slippery. 

Tough one with kids - just the final part

Views are amazing

It isn’t a trip to Killarney without hiking “The Crack”.  We do the climb up in 70 min.  Same time for the trek down.  This hike is extra busy this summer so start earlier to avoid the crowds and a full parking lot.  We started around 9:30.  Hike is well marked.  Proper footwear and water in a backpack is a must.  You will need your hands to help with some of the boulders.  Enjoy!

This is the first mountain my husband and I have ever tried, and it was definitely a challenge, even for us regular hikers. The view is well worth the climb. Be careful to watch for loose rocks before stepping your full weight onto them. Also watch for sharp rocks when scrambling up the boulders. 
On our way back, there was a black bear on the path. We made lots of noise (our voices, clapping, and knocking stones together) and he sauntered away. Be sure to make lots of noise, sing, whatever so you don’t startle a bear accidentally and end up in trouble!
Great trail! First 1/2 is easy, then once you start bouldering it’s intense. Do not do this trail in crap footwear! You will regret it.
Amazing hike. Bring lots of water, especially if it is a hot day.  Walking sticks also helped!  The last km or so gets pretty tough, but very fun!! Wear good hiking footwear.
The trail got progressively harder as it approached the crack. Beautiful view at the end.
No bugs and nice moderate hike. Went with 7 and 10 year old and they were faster than the parents! Pretty steep climb on big boulders at the end.

I'm not a hiker. My husband isn't either. I like walking and I'm reasonably fit. My husband tolerates walking and he's not fit. We're both overweight. I carried a heavy pack because I had to bring various things. We managed to complete this trail, but it was very hard. We intended to start the trail around 8. In the end, we got to the trail head at 10.20. It was already hot and humid by then. We took almost 20 breaks on the way up and 2 breaks on the way down. All in all, with time at the top, this hike took us 7 hours. The people who completed the trail the fastest had no packs, or just a bottle of water. But that is a compromise. There were people at the top who had got there reasonably fast, but they'd run out of water. Some of them had children with them. It was very hot and in the middle of the day. The views are nice, sure, but nothing I hadn't seen before. I'll give it 4 stars because the hike is nice and the terrain is interesting. I can see why people would find the views great. It's just I'm Swedish and I'm used to views like that. My favourite part was the first lake. It was like a mirror and looked fantastic. I'm going back on this trail to that lake in October, but I doubt I will complete any more of the trail than that. It was incredibly difficult for me to complete the trail. It took a lot. But once I'd completed the trail and was back at the car, I felt fine. I didn't have any aches or pains after, but the trail... it really took a lot out of me at the time. I was exhausted by the time we got to the top, but thankfully I quickly recovered and got back down again fine. I wore safety boots with steel caps (they worked great) and my husband wore hiking boots. He lost his footing once, but didn't get hurt. Bring more water than you think you will need, just in case. I know the trail is 7 km, but my husband's activity tracker recorded a distance of 14 km walked.
Nice path to the accent, the accent was fun, and the top was a great rest point to enjoy a beautiful view with a snack.

Our second time through the crack. This time we had two kids on our backs and our 5 year old on foot. Totally doable and a huge accomplishment for him. The walk back was the most difficult as he was sore and tired. 

In total it was about 5 hours with an hour rest at the top.

Last part is the tough
But overall amazing hike
It took us 3.5 hours
But take your time
It's a beautiful trail but the last 30-40 mins is difficult. If planning on hiking on a weekend, get there early otherwise there is no parking. Parking costs $15.50.

Incredible beautiful views once you complete the climb, well worth the effort.

Don’t miss this trail if you get the chance. 

This is rated moderate, it’s actually a very difficult climb up the crack, certainly not moderate. 

If it’s wet, it will be very dangerous.
Great view at the end of the trail. Hard climb close to the end with loose rocks and steep inclines.

Really nice hike, did it with 5yo and it was a bit challenging especially towards the Kidney lake, bit climbing but all had amazing time. definitely take hiking boots if you can as the rocks can be slippery even when dry, altho seen people doing this hike in birkenstocks ;)
Amazing

highly recommended. beautiful views
 3 hrs out and back with 45 mins uptop.
Awesome

Great trail! Quite buggy at the beginning but just come with bug spray and you’ll be ok! 
The views are incredible and well worth it- make sure to wear supportive shoes!

We did this hike three days ago, and it was absolutely beautiful. 

I'd recommend biking the first half of the trail if you're alble, since it's mostly flat and would bring you to the more interesting part of the hike a bit quicker. You could lock your bike to a tree, do the hike, then bike out once you're done. Walking it was still lovely though, so if that's your only option it's still a good one. 

We were at the top by around noon, but I'd highly recommend going earlier in the day to avoid having more hikers on the trail. That being said, once you get to the top it's pretty easy to find your own spot to enjoy the view with some privacy. 

Bring lots of water and a first aid kit. There are exposed roots the entire length of the trail, and there are moving rocks that you'll climb over as you near the crack. It's easy to find good hand & foot holds as you scramble up and over the boulders, but definitely test rocks out before trusting your full weight on them.

It's not great a great hike for young kids or pets, but we did see a lot of young families up there, so while it's not ideal, it's certainly doable. 

There are a ton of wild blueberries and juniper berries to pick too, so if you know your berries (and feel confident picking/eating the right ones) bring a small container to collect some goodies along the way!

Such an amazing view. Most of the trail was pretty easy with only the last km being difficult. Not including breaks it took my friend and I 3h to complete. There is alot of loose rocks and steep terrain with cell service only at the peak so I reccomend bringing a first aid kit just incase. 
If I were to do this hike again I would probally start hiking at 9am we went around 11am and it started to get very busy with lots of other hikers arriving as we were coming down. I definitely would not recommend this hike for young children and dogs unless u are prepared to carry them as some of the crevasses are very large.
Also do not forget that this is rattlesnake country so be weary.

Nice hike with a lot of climbing up the rocks. Footing is mostly easy to reach with only couple of dificult parts. We missed the trail in one part which led to some intense climbing but found our way back.  on the way back we took the trail and it was alright. We had a lot of fun, and the view is worth the climb.
We had water and snacks, which I recommend, but there were people without either. Couple of big dogs and preteen children climbed to the top too.
It took us almost 4 hours with 2 breaks. Check the weather forecast because people who were starting might have been caught by a bad storm.

Great trail - quite easy at the start but like other the end bit navigating is a bit difficult. Brought the dog and had to help him a bit but he was able to figure it out - a few others were up there too. Bug spray, water, and snacks are a necessity!

This is honestly so overhyped. If you’re fit it takes about 45 minutes each way. It’s not the most difficult trail in the world. It’s about 3.5-4K each way and only the last 2km are even rugged. The first part is wide enough to fit a truck and feels like a road. The climbing toward the summit is a lot of fun and the only challenging part. View from the top is gorgeous of course.

Beautiful trail. Definitely a bit difficult towards the end with lots of climbing with your hands. I would not recommend children or dogs but some made it well enough. Bring lots of water and snacks. Took us about 3 hours there and back (not including our stop at the top for lunch). I would def recommend!! (Also wear good shoes!!!)

Absolutely Fantastic Hike! Very technical as you climb many rocks and you have to follow markers so this map helped a ton cause it’s easy to get lost, but it’s well worth it! The crack part is very unique and a great time!

Fun trail but very technically challenging at the end and coming back down. I have patelofemoral syndrome in my right knee, and going down irritated it good. Did the trail in 4 hours, not including stop for lunch. You need good footwear, water, and snacks. We did this half pack to prep for another hike, but for the inexperienced people. Have a safety plan in place. Was talking with a Park Warden and they do 2-3 rescues a week. Also keep to the trail, we came off to a old section, but stopped and had to find the proper trail.

This is probably the most beautiful hike I’ve ever done! BUT! This trail is rated difficult for a reason. Make sure you leave enough time, 4 hrs is an accurate measure of how long it will take you to get to the top and back. You do have to do a difficult scramble to get to the top. The trail has been detoured and is longer, over 8 km now but slightly less steep (but right at the beginning, not at the actual rock climbing point). Make sure you give yourself at least 4 hrs before sunset when heading out and bring a lot of water. I would not take children or dogs on the trail, they would have to be carried up the rocky scramble. However I saw people with both dogs and children, I think they may stop at the first lookout but even that is a little difficult. Whoever can do this is 2.5 hrs is either an Olympian or isn’t going all the way to top.
This is a great trail with amazing views. It’s a true hiking trail with a lot of rocks to climb over. Definitely NOT good for dogs or kids the closer you get to the top.

Oh gorgeous! Would definitely do this again. First off - the park rates this as hard/difficult. The first part of the trail is so easy, it seems service vehicles park in there. The second half is moderate then it turns into a hard scramble up rocks, which is SO fun! We had the best weather with minimal bugs and slightly overcast at the peak with only like 5 droplets of rain. Therefore we sat and enjoyed our lunch with the view without worry of heat or sunburn. Perfect day.

Please be prepared with good footwear and ensure you have good knees to do this! You will use your hands to climb, be ready!

Rated only as 4 stars due to discrepancy with the park rating and as it is definitely not a standard moderate trail! I do believe it to be harder than moderate at the peak and that rating could mislead someone.

Amazing trail and view. If you are looking for a good 4-5hr hike this is perfect. It's great for experienced hikers, but beginners can also do this and take it slow. If it's a hot day make sure to bring lots of water as the top 500m is full of sun and rock. Everything was clearly marked with the red ticker.

Amazing trail and great views up top. First quarter of trail is on flat land with some aggressive bugs, but not as many bugs for the rest of the trail. Rock scrambles are for the second half of the trail, which was quite fun! 

The park rates this as a "difficult" trail which I agree due to climbing rocks.
Great trail for a beginner. Seems like a casual stroll at the beginning, but gets gradually more difficult. The view from the top is spectacular and well worth the moderate effort.

A challenging hike but the view is 100% worth it. Bring lots of water, wear long sleeves and pants for the bugs, and wear good shoes. There is a section where you will have to climb up some rocks, so make sure that you’re in decent shape before attempting this climb!

Stunning views! I’m from BC and I was surprised by how well maintained and well marked the trails in this parks were. This is a gorgeous park, surrounded by small lakes, white rock formations and varying terrain. The only downside are the small swaps surrounding the entrances, which means lots of mosquitos and bugs. I wore shorts and the next day I had itchy bumps all over my legs. Bug spray is a must, along with good hiking shoes for the slippery rock formations. One more thing to be aware of is that the rocks are incredibly sharp - my friend had a bad cut just from gripping the rocks wrong. Be careful and enjoy the views!
Most amazing scenic view from the top but you have to get to the top of the Crack to enjoy the fullness of it. If you love a great hike, this is well with your time. Bring water, snacks and camera!

Things you'll need are sturdy shoes, water, lunch for the picnic on top, bug spray (!!!) and sunblock. Absolutely breath taking views. We went with a medium sized dog and he couldn't do the last part, but we saw that another dog did it... so maybe it's possible. It's very easy at the beginning, then a little moderate (save your energy) and then there is about 10 minutes of proper rock climbing. I will say going up seems easier than going down. So enjoy that lunch! All of us were a little sore and tired after the hike and we loved it! This hike is a must!!!
Challenging but worth it
Absolutely beautiful! worth the climb and every ounce of sweat!
Saw at moose on the road out there! The scramble at the top of the hike was more technical than expected, which made for a fun hike! Very buggy at the beginning.
I wish it was a loop. Hiking the same way back made it a little boring.
Love this trail.  It can be quite busy with all of the tourists in Killarney but the view is worth the hike.   Small children might have difficulty with the last leg being pretty rocky.
Undoubtedly, one of the best day hikes in Ontario. Lots of variety and your efforts are rewarded with an exceptional view from the ridge.

Great trail with varied terrain and a spectacular vista from the top of the ridge. My mini poodle was able to ascend without much difficulty and was carried down for one of the rockier portions of the descent, so I think it may be challenging, though doable, for dogs and small children. The one fatal flaw with an otherwise fantastic hike is the enormous hordes of hungry black flies in the late spring/early summer, which only increases the further you ascend, making it near-impossible to actually enjoy your surroundings. Beware of the bugs if you intend on visiting during the warmer months!

Amazing view. The rock cut is a little steep and dangerous for children/dogs but I’ve seen both do it before. Great elevation and variety of terrain. Mossy forest, open meadows, shaded trees and open rock faces for a great panoramic view.

beautiful view!!! definitely worth going to. used slip on cleats for ice.. definitely needed.

 parking meter was down.

**This is outdated**
The crack trail has been rerouted. There are signs along the trail indicating the changes. The new route is honestly better as the incline is not as intense but it adds a little more distance.
That being said this is the best trail in Ontario, best way to do it is with a small backback for snacks and water and leave early in the morning and enjoy lunch on top. Ive done the crack in all weather conditions in all seasons and every one still makes the journey worth it.
Phenomenal.
great trail...it gets pretty tough closer to the top but well worth it!
Amazing trail, not to be missed.

Great view once you’re at the top! Pretty challenging and was tired by the end but it was worth it. Definitely needed hiking boots. Wouldn’t recommend doing it in the rain as there is lots of rocks that would be slippery

Starts as an easy well maintained trail then turns into a rocky climb with lots of white granite. Be careful, rocks are slippery when damp! Beautiful, was great to eat lunch on the peak! Currently there is a 600m detour in place because they are repairing part of the trail.

Awesome hike. Scramble up rocks near the top is not for those who don't like uneven footing. You need your hands for several spots. I recommend having a meal at the top to recharge and take in the view.
Nice hike. Start early though since it can be really crowdy.
Beautiful views, fun trail to scramble on - completed it during our 4 day thru-hike of La Cloche.
Great!
Great Trail.  The new detours make the trail a lot easier.  Accessing the top with a dog is somewhat of a challenge due to rocky conditions.  Views are awesome.
Great Trail with an excellent view at the top!
Long, variable terrain. Incredible views at the top

Spectacular views. No mosquitoes made it even better.

I recommend hiking 1 hour or so northeast for another amazing easterly views.
A favorite hike of ours! Love looking down on sites of past canoe trips.
Such a beautiful trail, my dogs love it. Lots of climbing which I love but also lots of flat surfaces to walk as well.
the views are absolutely stunning. photos cannot capture the beauty of the view points.
Unbelievable view at the top. 100% worth it. Give yourself a good 4 hours to complete.

Wow. The view was amazing! Be prepared to spend lots of time at the top taking in the views.  it was a warm day and we passed some hot and exhausted large dogs on close to the top- not sure why people would do that to their dogs. They must have had to carry them over the rocks in the last section.
great trail the view at the end makes the work to get there worth it 2 thumbs up
So worth the mud and bugs. The view from the top was incredible.

As good as it gets. Took about 2 hours up and down with moderate fitness + time for photos. Rocky towards the top, but only for a short stint and certainly not insurmountable.

Bugs were bad when we arrived at 9am; long sleeves and pants, and bug net were a lifesaver. It was much better on the way down. Either start later, or come prepared. We took a detour on the way back to follow la cloche toward George lake, but turned back shortly after as the bugs got heavier.
Great trail, super buggy but worth it for the views.
easier than I thought, wear lots of bug repellent if hiking here in the summer. views atop are very nice.
A real treat. They're updating the trail at one point to take a bit of a different route, it's quite well marked, and probably adds about half a kilometer

Loved this trail. Not as difficult as you may think although you do need to use both hands and feet together at some locations to get up and over some very large rocks. The view from the top is totally worth the effort.

Great hike, begins easy, challenging at the end.  If you take it steady it is no problem, our 9 1/2 year old border collie climbed the rocks, although it did quieten her down, which is a challenge. Was hot when we went so took plenty of water.
Did it in 2 hours yesterday. Bugs were bad in some spots.
Beautiful, bug suit advised.
It’s a harder trail, but definitely worth it!
I loved this trail. Sometimes rocky which makes it interesting yet still some boardwalks to walk on too! Perfect length. Took me just short of 3 hours.

First and foremost, wear study shoes and leave the dresses at home.  This trail is a good mixed hike with packed trail,  roots and bridges and scrambling up rocks to the peak.  Been wanting to do this one for a while and it doesn’t disappoint.
Some parts are pretty steep. Not so easy on the knees but the end point view was worth it!

Excellent hike with stunning views. Definitely a moderate to hard hike, depending on your fitness level. Mostly flat for the first 2.5km and then it starts to ramp up quite quickly. Important to take certain parts slow and pace yourself, especially once the rock scramble begins. 100% worth it for the gorgeous views.
Excellent hike.  A bit muddy in the flat sections, not a surprise for this spring.  Also lots of bugs , but hey it’s June.

The forest portion of the trail was a bit muddy at points but it's easy to go around, and there are some obvious alternative paths to do so. It is rather buggy but it's that time of year. There were a lot of black flies as you climb to the peak, I would suggest long sleeves/pants and a bug net for your face. 

Overall, a beautiful and challenging hike. All Trails lists this as moderate difficulty, while the sign at the start lists it as difficult (probably for the climb up/down through the crack itself).
So many dang bugs. Bug nets, jackets and stink location are a must!!

Probably one of the most beautiful hikes I have ever done. Camped a couple days out here on a camp site and spent a a bunch of time up at the top watching the landscape . It’s a huge up hill for the average hiker and the trail is always not so obvious . Just have to keep a steady eye for markers and where the beaten path lay . Is well worth it to see a mountain of white quartz. Next time will be much further in to the park . This place is massive
Bugs were bad once you stopped moving and the last 30 minutes is hard work, but it’s all worth the view!!

Lord of the Ringish.  Amazing.  You have to really look for the markers as is not obvious sometimes but in a fun way .  Steep climb over fallen boulders near the top. Rewarded with an absolutely spectacular view.  One of most unique and best trails in Ontario.
It was a great hike through the woods and the views were nice from the top. Trail was muddy in some sections, but there were often side trails around them.
Great hiking trail in Killarney. Moderate to difficult depending on conditioning but well worth it. Hiked it in summer and fallb last year. Truly amazing views and a great workout!
I really enjoyed this hike, it was steep at some points and had to get creative with the footing but the view at the top was gorgeous and a good spot for a lunch break!
Amazing views from the top
beautiful view, fun rocky sections of the trail, overall favourite hike in ontario!

Did this hike mid December, about of Foot of snow on the ground and was beautiful, amazing view from the top after climbing up a bunch of rocks/boulders, glad we had snow pants on for the climb down as there were a lot of icy rocks and we slid down on our back sides. 14$ parking in the lot at trail head
Awesome foliage. Our Brittany spaniel made it to the top. A must see.

Stunning and amazing trail. combined rocks, water and beautiful flore. 
not extremely hard but can't be accessible for everyone because of the last part (you will need the help of your hands to reach the top, but if you are fit enought to reach this point you can finish it)  the effort is SO worth it!!
Beautiful scenery throughout the entire trail. Difficult rock scrambles in parts but overall a moderate trail.
Definitely a great hike! Worth the trek for the view! - Speaking from an inexperienced hiker, this trail was manageable. A moderate-hard hike depending on your fitness level.

Good hike. hit the trail at 8:30 back by 12 with about 45 minutes at the peak.

for at 3/4 of the trail is easy going with some short but steep inclines and rocks to climb.

last 1/4 is more boulder climbing. to the top of the cliff. would not recommend doing the full hike for children under 6. instead I would go to the first lookout that is open. they will think it is the top and you have amazing views. from there is you look to your right you will see a cliff about 250 m away with a similar height. that is the end point for the crack. 

hiking shoes needed. recommend min of 2L of water or a water filter there are many streams you can pull from.

My absolute favorite hike in Ontario (so far). First 2.5km were a breeze - fairly flat and wide, easy to follow and peaceful. The next bit was tougher - you are climbing some big rocky/root-filled hills (starting to hit some amazing views) until the 3.5km (or so mark) - a final accession up the crack. I had to put my camera away to scamper up the steep steep rocks. Spectacular views at the top. Stopped for lunch there. It was pretty busy (we encountered 15 or more small groups or pairs of hikers in the 3.5 hours we were there) even though we went on a Tuesday morning. I loved this hike. Gorgeous in the fall. Would love to do the whole La Cloche Sillouhette Loop next!

Depending on your fitness level and hiking experience I would rate this hike as a mod-hard trail. Absolutely worth the climb for the view. The beginning walkthrough is nice and easy then the climbing begins. A few small climbs and descents until the main climb through the crack up to the viewpoint.
Amazing hike, much preffered over Silver Peak even!

Great trail! However only certain dogs can do this trail, be ready to boost them from rock to rock. Not that dog friendly in my opinion - left my two Bernese mountain dogs at the lodge, no way they would’ve been able to do this trail.
j4
Fun and challenging hike. Great views.

I hiked this trail with my dog in May. We started the trail around 2pm. It took us about 3.5 hours in total with stops along the way. The trail wasn't too overcrowded since it was a week before the May long weekend. 
It's a beautiful trail, and the view at the top definitely makes the climb worth it! It can be tough climbing some of the larger rocks along the route, and it isn't always clear where the trail is. There are lots of places to stop and take in the views along the route. Would definitely recommend this trail!

The crack was a great trail. Took about an hour and a half to climb up. A lot more climbing and scramble than expected but not too hard. Spent over an hour at the top. The view was well worth it! Took about an hour on the way down. Try and go in the morning because it does get busy. If you bring a small dog expect to be carrying it at some points.
Amazing views!  Make sure to wear good tread hiking shoes/boots.  Rocks can be slippery to climb on when wet.
beautiful view at top specially in the fall.  have been 3 times. will keep going!
Although at times challenging, this trail is unique and offers unbelievable viewpoints! Would definitely recommend :)
Great trail - enough of a challenge and beautiful views!
Great trail. Nice views
Fairly active path, met lots of people, is quite the climb but it super worth it. Extremely unique and a little challenging.

Hiked this trail August 5, 2018. Started out early, around 8:30 am and met several people coming back on the way up. The first 2 km are a walk in the park but it then it gets more challenging as you get into more up hill hiking over lots of tree roots. From here it moves into scrambling over rocks up to the top of a hill (just a warm up to the Crack). You then have a decent and back into an uphill hike over tree roots before getting to the Crack. The Crack is a steep uphill scramble over more rocks but there is always a place to get a good foothold. It took about 2 hours in total to get to the top.
The view at the top is awesome but it started to get crowded around 11 am making it difficult to get good shots with foreground interest that didn’t have people in it. 
Started back around noon and were back at the car around 1:30. The last kilometre was difficult even though it was easy trail. (Probably due to the heat and humidity).
The trail is well marked but you need to look up to see the markers. We were glad we took 3 1/2 litres of water. We drank 3 litres. 
It would be a great trail in the fall or a great place to catch an awesome sunrise or sunset for those with experience.
We would rate the trail difficult.
Nice hike, nice views. Definitely doesn’t deserve the hard rating however.
It’s a weekly staple hike during July and August for us. Great way to kick start a work out and maintain your fitness level!

Challenging hike overall - lots of rocks to climb over and through with steep ascension close to the lookout.  Absolutely amazing view at the top and worth the challenge.  Saw families and dogs on the trail.  You’ll need a partner to help your dog over the toughest points to avoid injury. Going down is tricky so make sure you take your time.  A bucket list hike for any nature lover!

Challenging and rewarding. We did the hike with our two kids in backpacks. (3 years and 15 months). It was challenging at times but doable for sure. Saw lots of families and groups on the way there and back. Would recommend having one adult per child of hiking with kids. Going down was far more difficult than getting up. Views are paramount. Really great hike.

I would not rate this trail as “moderate” and Lake of The Woods as “hard.” This trail’s elevations reserve it for more serious hikers.  You can bring older children that are accustom to hiking with proper footwear.  The views are remarkable and the traffic is light.
Amazing hike with breathtaking views ...... takes about three hours there and back and as an hour to enjoy the views up top......

The Crack at Killarney is without a doubt one of the best hikes in Ontario. It was a tad confusing at one point to figure out where to go. I know they re-routed it since I've done it in 2018. Really great trail, really easy at the beginning through the forest and gets more difficult the closer you get to the "Crack"! Bring a lot of water, sunscreen, and a hat... the last stretch you're walking on exposed outcropping of granite and its HOT. There's also black flies in the forest around spring/summer. The view at the top is really awesome.
Was a great hike. As others have said the first part of the trail was very buggy and I got eaten alive, however the view from the top was stunning- a nice spot for lunch before heading back down.
Good hike. Only the last part is scrambly. Good views from the top. It took me 2:40 hrs to complete the hike.

Age 37 male, 135lbs. Did this with my 35-year-old gf. I found it really easy. If this is labelled 'hard', it kind of makes the 'hard' designation useless, since there are countless trails I've done that are much, much, much more challenging. It's still a nice little hike... simple walk on a path through the woods for the first half, then some nice going up rocks until one gets to the top. Nice views up there of the surrounding area. We went on a nice sunny weekday in mid-June, before school finished for the year. There were people certainly, but not too busy, starting at 11am. Didn't see any wildlife. Bugs were annoying and got some bites despite multiple OFF sprayings, but not horrible. If we had put on our nets and all that, we probably would not have been bitten at all.
Without question one of my favourite trails. Some fun scrambling rewarded with incredible views!
Awesome walk lots of fun..
i did the trail all the way to the crack didnt do the full loop but the 3 hour trip there and back was worth it amazing veiw just very up hill and treacherous
awesome hike.  first 2km ho hum forest walk. final push is craggy steep and awesome. gotta have your wits about you on the steep terrain.
Amazing trail, especially in the fall. I would love to do it again - every year
The hike was very busy with people. Some parts of the hike were very hard and almost impossible to navigate, need good foot wear and stamina for this one.

Always love this trail. 
View is worth the work!
Loved it - just a little tricky near the top (loose rock) but all and all very doable and a great view. Some nice stands of hemlocks and pines too for the tree lovers like me.

Great day hike. Relatively flat at first then a gradual ascent that is somewhat exposed. If you are doing this in the middle of the day bring sunscreen. Spectacular view from the top and wroth the climb. Not many hikes like this around Ontario that are so easily accessible.

Started on this trail around 9:45 am and it took roughly 4 hours to the Crack and back. Due to the ice build up, and packed snow the trail did get a little slippery and hard to maneuver, especially when going up and down hill.  I wouldn’t recommend doing this hill in the late winter/early spring with younger children. It was a beautiful hike up, and the view alone was worth the extra time it took to get there. Definitely a physically demanding trail, but the laughs along way made it worth it.

Awesome trail. Only gets a bit tricky as you start to ascend. The first bit isn't too bad but the last bit up
The crack is a little more rough. Amazing views at the top so worth it. Slippery when wet but those leaves on the ground are sneakier. Would not do this with children under 10. Says its dog friendly but the last bit would be less so.
One of my most favorite trails in Ontario. Definitely do it! The difficulty depends on your physical state. I hiked it with my 10 year old daughter and she didn't think the hike was challenging.
Hiked twice with my mastiff this year! What a great trail with beautiful views
Beautiful, would go again and again ♡

my family hiked the crack. very hard but beautiful views. We left early a.m and hiked all day. we packed a lunch,drinks,first aid. we hiked it once with our 12 year old, very hard for the kids. dogs are aloud but on leash. also you half to pay for parking. It is a great hiked but defenetly all day for a family. very busy during the weekend even during the week popular place. ppl were somewhat friendly passing by and shared the path once we got to tight spots. very fun defenetly a good work out but you'll sleep good when home! I reccomend doing some stretchs prior to hike and afterwards. bring your camera! proper shoes needed. rocks are slippery!  took us from 11am to 6pm hiking at a steady pace.

Easy at first then proceeds to get a little more difficult with the climbs. Beautiful hike that takes about 2 hours each way. Would not recommend going after any rainfall as the rocks can be quite slippery!
Beautiful easy until the end when you have to scramble to the top. Forth the effort
great trail with a couple of challenging spots.  At one point I went off trail a bit and  my dog fell off a ledge (he was unharmed thank goodness), so be careful with your four legged friends.
Very fun and challenfing hike. Bit of scrambling near the top. Beautiful views and lots of space at the lookout!
The view at the top is amazing.  Must do again in the Fall.
Easily one of my favorite hikes in Ontario. The view from the top is breathtaking!
A must see and do in Killarney . Amazing views from the top .

Parking was 14$ which was a drag but the trail was beautiful. The path was smooth for about 2km then the incline started. Half way point was nice rest area then going up to the top was very rocky not good for large packs. Views from above were great, you could see 2 lakes and the trail up.
I really love going out to Killarney to hike this trail! Very beautiful at the top
Loved the hike to the top. Its a moderate to difficult trail in some places, however, the view on the top is amazing. Worth the hike!!
Nice trail with some difficult boulder hopping near the summit. We did this trail on a cool, overcast 64 degree morning. Loved it.

extraordinary
you need to be fit to do it
watch your steps on the rocks before reaching the peak
Trail is marked poorly. The couple that came back my way said they got lost too. It is a very challenging climb towards the end. Would definitely do it again.
Kids loved it ..Can't wait to do it again
a little tricky at parts but well worth the trip. will definitely come back.

My dad and I hiked this after a greuling day of canoing/portaging. We were already pretty beat, but saw the sign for a hike and thought "hey cool lets try it". We went up in our keen sandals and a nalgene each and had no idea how rocky it would be. Needless to say the advil went down easy that night!. I do recommend proper footwear (we were ok but barely), but probably the most beautiful hike ive ever done in Ontario.
Did this in the winter. Was amazing overall. Veiws were the best.
One of the most beautiful hikes I've had the pleasure of doing. It's challenging, but to get to the top of the Crack and see the view, it's rewarding
amaizing hike and view :-)
easy flat walk at first, and then a steady uphill climb for a couple of kilometers... but so incredibly worth it!!!

Very close to Carlyle road 7km from the main gate heading East youll see 2 red posts. This is your entrence to the hike. There is a sign 1.5km in that says 2km to top it is more like 2.5km and the sign that says 1km to trail head is 1.5km to trail head. I gpsed it at 8km round trip

The hike starts very simple for the first 2.5-3km the last 100-200m I'd grade as a class 2-3 scramble and I would not suggest on a raining day. Experienced hikers can do round trip in 2 hours with water breaks and a nice little snack at top. Would not recomend for those afraid of heights

We did the Crack then La Cloche, then we went to Little Superior Lake, we left the parking at 9:30 and arrive to the Little Superior Lake at noon (no long breaks) we were absolutly alone on all the trail (except the first part to the Crack which is The main stream trail in this Park) but after that : nobody! 
Great views, landscape, wild animals... Perfect!
we spend a few time on the Lake. I drunk Lake water because we had not enough for the way back (very good water and no stomach ache) 
the way back was the same except for the part from the Crack to the parking which was crowded sadly.
so The Crack yes but start as early as you can and continue to the Little Superior Lake otherwise you will miss the best.

Camped at site 48 in April. 5 and a half hour hike total to the site with 50lbs of gear. The Crack (2.5-3hrs) offered such a phenomenal view. You can see Georgian Bay in the distance and the drop off the Crack is breath taking. Challenging hike but very rewarding. Wear proper footwear and there are steep sections and some very loose rock. A must see!
Have hiked this a few years on thanksgiving weekend. Great view with the fall colours. Cracktastic! Crackarific! Cracktabulous!

This is a beautiful hike with some steep inclines towards the end into the crack. Hiking shoes are a must-have to get a good grip while climbing through the rocks in the crack. But once you're through it, the view is just breathtaking! Bug spray is necessary too, or those hats with nets. Took us 4 hours to complete.
